Heading levels, line endings, outer document spacing and source-relative Markdown links are normalized here; code and mathematical expressions are preserved.

### Calculus–geometry pilot results

The corrected equality interpretation has a working mathematical and Python realization. This pilot produced exact rational geometry, differentiated affine projection, a bounded global polynomial compatibility checker and repaired root sensitivities. In the tested fixed representations, it did not demonstrate a new mathematical principle or a broad advantage over matched controls. Learned collapse features, task-conditioned geometry and nonlinear realization maps were not evaluated in this pilot; their usefulness is not settled by these results.

The [follow-up opportunity analysis](/home/vardan/dev/projects/omnibias/docs/calculus-geometry-opportunities.md) audits this scope, distinguishes earlier learned-profile experiments, and derives concrete directions for constrained predictions, geometric PFNs, manifolds and Boolean circuits.

The completed [research campaign](/home/vardan/dev/projects/omnibias/docs/calculus-geometry-campaign.md) adds independent
replay, fresh-seed constrained TabPFN confirmation, physical-sensitivity and
finite-calibration-step certificates, and a global monotone-energy verifier.
Its evidence and conclusions are separate from this earlier pilot.

The [derivations](/home/vardan/dev/projects/omnibias/docs/calculus-geometry-pilot.md) state the proofs and limitations; the [API guide](/home/vardan/dev/projects/omnibias/docs/affine-geometry.md) contains executable examples. [Machine-readable summary](/home/vardan/dev/projects/omnibias/docs/benchmarks/calculus_geometry_pilot.json).

#### Scientific ML

Six cases use two finite characteristic-wave families and seeds 101, 211, 307. The periodic wave system is satisfied by construction; initial data are inferred from noisy observations rather than supplied as exact constraints. All methods below share the same restricted exact solution family. The neural control trains a linear output layer over fixed sinusoidal features.

| Method | Mean held-out u RMSE | Maximum PDE residual | Mean setup + solve (s) |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| `direct_characteristic_ls` | 0.004845836 | 1.67e-15 | 0.00016232 |
| `svd_nullspace_ls` | 0.004845836 | 8.25e-14 | 0.00518564 |
| `omnibias_projected_ls` | 0.004845836 | 4.79e-14 | 0.00263937 |
| `ordinary_qr_projected_ls` | 0.004845836 | 8.3e-14 | 0.000655202 |
| `matched_sine_network_adam` | 0.00492675 | 1.37e-15 | 0.156163 |

Direct coefficient least squares solves this family efficiently. The affine projection does not improve its fitted solution. Setup includes each method's factorization and projection construction; common representation/observation-array construction and imports are outside these small component timings. There are no repeated isolated timing samples, so the numbers do not support general speed claims.

The polynomial checker certifies a cubic wave's global derivative/PDE/initial-data identities and rejects an algebraically PDE-feasible but incompatible derivative section. Separately, pointwise projection makes a first-order PDE residual nearly zero while leaving contact defects of magnitude 0.5. Thus geometric intersections in derivative coordinates need a realizability condition.

The [20 October re-audit](/home/vardan/dev/projects/omnibias/docs/unification-research-audit.md) distinguishes these
examples explicitly. The pointwise edit is incompatible with the retained
value field, although its derivative vector alone integrates to a different
field. A separate nonzero-curl example cannot be integrated at all. The
successful global compatible reconstruction remains valid; these counterexamples
do not reject every geometric correction.

#### Tabular learning

Exact rational affine-subspace recovery classifies 58 fresh on-plane and 58 off-plane points correctly. Perturbing each positive measurement by an exact 1/1000 off the plane, while retaining its latent positive label, gives zero positive recall. This tests measurement sensitivity of that fixed exact detector; it does not rule out equality decisions after nonanalytic learned embeddings such as ReLU.

The noisy-data experiment imposes four artificial fixed equalities in a 16-dimensional hidden representation and uses a separate prediction head. These equalities encode no medical domain knowledge. Validation chooses learning rate/depth and checkpoint; preprocessing uses training rows only.

| Dataset | Method | Mean test log loss | Mean test accuracy |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: |
| breast_cancer | `omnibias_projection` | 0.07966957 | 0.9736842 |
| breast_cancer | `ordinary_qr_projection` | 0.07966957 | 0.9736842 |
| breast_cancer | `absorbed_projection_head` | 0.07966957 | 0.9736842 |
| breast_cancer | `unconstrained_mlp` | 0.08376703 | 0.9707602 |
| breast_cancer | `catboost` | 0.08223323 | 0.9824561 |
| noisy_oblique_geometry | `omnibias_projection` | 0.4450984 | 0.8211382 |
| noisy_oblique_geometry | `ordinary_qr_projection` | 0.4450984 | 0.8211382 |
| noisy_oblique_geometry | `absorbed_projection_head` | 0.4450984 | 0.8211382 |
| noisy_oblique_geometry | `unconstrained_mlp` | 0.4523648 | 0.8146341 |
| noisy_oblique_geometry | `catboost` | 0.4453394 | 0.8195122 |

Native projection, ordinary QR and an absorbed-head equivalent network agree within 2.39e-15 in held-out probability. Their 20-step independent AdamW comparison also agrees in values, gradients and parameters. The modest pilot differences from the free MLP or boosting therefore do not establish a collapse-specific learning mechanism. A fixed projection immediately before a free affine head can be absorbed into that head.

Tree models are saved using CatBoost's official JSON format and replayed without refitting, alongside stored neural states and held-out predictions. Two numerical datasets and three splits cannot establish broad tabular superiority.

#### Optimization and LP

The pilot contains 9 bounded LPs and 36 explicitly regularized QPs. All 275 independent reference/witness checks pass. HiGHS finds LP active sets; subsequent linear solves and affine projections are reported conditional on those sets, not as full LP solvers.

LP optimizer cost sensitivities are locally zero inside the fixed active region; constraint-RHS sensitivities are nonzero and agree with independent finite differences. At an active-set transition the optimizer jumps, and nonuniqueness is retained explicitly. Infeasibility has a Farkas witness.

| Family | Candidate | Maximum solution error | Maximum cost-gradient error | Maximum relative cost-gradient error |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| lp | omnibias_solver | 1.85e-09 | — | — |
| lp | omnibias_layer | 1.85e-09 | 5.57e-09 | — |
| qp | omnibias_solver | 6.99e-06 | — | — |
| qp | omnibias_layer | 6.99e-06 | 0.628 | 4.05e-05 |

The existing barrier layer's approximation error increases as QP regularization shrinks. Reference-check success is distinct from candidate accuracy; candidate errors remain visible in the summary. CVXPYlayers was unavailable and was not benchmarked. These cases establish neither faster generic LP solution nor differentiability at hard active-set transitions.

#### Additional mathematical experiment: every continuous bias

The unshipped certificate prototype considers fixed-direction atoms \(\psi_b(x)=(x-b)_+^2\), \(b\in[0,1]\), and minimizes coefficient total variation subject to finite point observations. This is a continuous-dictionary convex measure problem. Exact primal feasibility gives an upper bound. Exact global pricing of \(g(b)=\sum_i q_i\psi_b(x_i)\) makes a scaled dual feasible over every permitted bias and gives a lower bound. Each pricing cell is quadratic, so endpoints and rational stationary points exhaust its extrema.

For data \(x=(1,2)\), \(y=(1/4,9/4)\), endpoint-only atoms have optimum \(3/2\). The atom at \(b=1/2\) fits with coefficient cost \(1\). The dual \(q=(-3,1)\) appears feasible on endpoint biases, but its correlation is \(-2b^2+2b+1\), whose true maximum is \(3/2\). Scaling to \((-2,2/3)\) proves the lower bound \(1\), matching the exactly recovered one-atom upper bound. This is a global optimum within the stated restricted dictionary, not unrestricted neural-network optimization.

![Exact continuous-bias pricing and two fitting representations](/home/vardan/dev/projects/omnibias/docs/img/research/continuous_bias_certificate.svg)

Both fields in the figure fit the two observations. The certificate concerns their optimization objective, not accuracy between unobserved points or a PDE solution. Distributionally, the classical identity \(D_x^3\psi_b=2\delta_b\) connects these atoms to sparse sources.

The independent replayer verifies 25 retained rows across seven cases. The four-step exchange closes 2 cases, including the zero target; 1 has a positive gap and 4 initial dictionaries cannot produce a dual certificate. Known generating atoms provide labeled fallback upper bounds in those cases, and do not count as recovered solutions. The 21/101-point dense-grid controls close 6/7 and 6/7 cases; remaining cases retain positive gaps. Thus the exchange is not promoted as a superior solver.

The measure formulation, spline KKT conditions and exchange method are established. See [Bach 2017](https://jmlr.org/papers/v18/14-546.html), [Parhi–Nowak 2021](https://jmlr.org/papers/v22/20-583.html) and [Pilanci–Ergen 2020](https://proceedings.mlr.press/v119/pilanci20a.html). The scoped addition is an exact checker that detects a finite-grid certificate being incorrectly extended to all continuous biases. [Complete path-neutral certificate record](/home/vardan/dev/projects/omnibias/docs/benchmarks/continuous_bias_certificate.json).

Outputs refuse overwrite. Replays check source/dependency/lock fingerprints and the complete frozen case matrix, then recompute identities, model predictions and witness arithmetic without retraining or retiming. Source changes require fresh output directories. The initial pre-hardening run is retained separately; the final run includes complete-matrix checks and serialized tree replay.

Preserve the reusable geometry and compatibility primitives, with their tests and explicit limitations. The strongest continuation question is whether corrections that preserve a realizable field, or certificates over continuous parameters, help a workload beyond ordinary coefficient algebra. That needs its own strong control and measurable advantage. The [opportunity analysis](/home/vardan/dev/projects/omnibias/docs/calculus-geometry-opportunities.md) also identifies learned geometric and Boolean architectures outside this pilot; none is refuted by the fixed-projection equivalence.

## Appendix 005: omnibias/docs/calculus-geometry-opportunities.md

Source: [omnibias/docs/calculus-geometry-opportunities.md](/home/vardan/dev/projects/omnibias/docs/calculus-geometry-opportunities.md). Original SHA256: `ce9dde73af1810d02c5b453f23c91971f807454cbb746609b7e926e7609f01ac`.

This is the complete source note at compilation time. Its original experiment date, protocol, limitations and historical status apply; later corrections in the overview and subsequent audit notes take precedence. Heading levels, line endings, outer document spacing and source-relative Markdown links are normalized here; code and mathematical expressions are preserved.

### Calculus and geometry research opportunities

The four-hour pilot validates fixed representations and their derivatives. It does not evaluate the whole proposed family of learned geometric models. A useful architecture can combine established mathematics in a new way, but the connection between neuron derivatives, geometric sets and differential equations does not itself establish architectural novelty or a learning advantage. This assessment distinguishes those questions and identifies experiments that could answer them.

#### What the pilot can establish

| Experiment | Actual construction | What remains outside its scope |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Wave system | Fixed characteristic sine/cosine features; fit output coefficients | Learned directions, biases, derivative dictionaries, interfaces and nonlinear realization maps |
| Noisy tabular data | Fixed artificial affine constraints immediately before a free affine prediction head | Task-conditioned constraints, nonlinear distance features, mixtures of manifolds and PFN pretraining |
| LP and QP | Existing solvers plus sensitivities conditional on the discovered active set | Learned presolvers, active-set proposals and amortized optimization across related problems |

There is no obvious arithmetic defect explaining the reported equivalences. For a fixed affine projection \(h\mapsto Ph+q\) and a free affine head,

\[
W(Ph+q)+d=(WP)h+(Wq+d).
\]

That is an algebraic equivalence. The factorization can change optimization or regularization relative to an unconstrained parameterization, but the independent control can reproduce those choices too. The identity does not eliminate nonlinear distance features, input-dependent projections, or constraints on the actual prediction target.

The wider repository has already tested learned band profiles, beyond this pilot. The stronger [profile controls](/home/vardan/dev/projects/omnibias/docs/benchmarks/profile_controls_study.json) include 360 selected evaluations: learned Laplace profiles beat the learned collapsed profile on all six dataset means and 29 of 30 matched splits. Those results argue against treating the particular collapsed profile as intrinsically superior. They do not evaluate geometric PFN priors, cardinality circuits or coherent manifold models.

The precise conclusion is: **the tested constructions did not demonstrate a new mathematical principle or a broad advantage over matched controls; the broader proposed architectures remain research questions.**

#### The underlying objects have direct precedents

An exact equality neuron means precisely

\[
E_{w,b}(x)=\mathbf 1\{w^Tx=b\}.
\]

This definition is preserved. It is not replaced by a sigmoid band. [Koiran and Sontag, 1997, printed page 196, Lemma 6](https://www.sontaglab.org/FTPDIR/quadratic-vc.pdf) explicitly use linear and equality gates, with equality output one only at zero. [Kilic, Sima and Bruck, 2024](https://arxiv.org/html/2402.08751v1) define exactly \(\mathbf1\{w^TX=b\}\), compose such gates into circuits, and study geometric representations of \(AX=b\) on Boolean inputs. These sources rule out invention of the predicate itself, without deciding the value of a particular training method.

The calculus connection is also explicit in prior work. For a unit normal w, distributionally,

\[
\Delta\operatorname{ReLU}(w^Tx-b)=\delta_H,
\qquad H=\{x:w^Tx=b\},
\]

where \(\delta_H\) integrates test functions over the hyperplane. For general nonzero w the factor is \(\|w\|\delta_H\). [Parhi and Nowak, 2021, Figure 3](https://jmlr.org/papers/volume22/20-583/20-583.pdf) explicitly maps a ReLU network to hyperplane impulse sheets, then to atoms encoding orientations and biases. A surface measure and an equality indicator share a set but are different mathematical objects.

Normalized bias differences also have a precise scope. For \(\sigma\in C^k\) on a neighborhood of z,

\[
\lim_{h\to0}h^{-k}\sum_{j=0}^{k}(-1)^{k-j}{k\choose j}
\sigma(z+jh)=\sigma^{(k)}(z).
\]

The signed coefficients and normalization matter. Merely making k+1 neurons' biases coincide gives their summed activation, not automatically its kth derivative. These are classical finite differences and confluent representations. A useful implementation might improve conditioning of nearly cancelling neurons, but must compare to stable divided differences and direct derivative-activation features.

For PDE representations, [EPGP](https://proceedings.mlr.press/v202/harkonen23a.html) constructs priors that exactly satisfy systems of linear constant-coefficient PDEs. [Local extreme learning machines](https://arxiv.org/abs/2012.02895) fix hidden parameters and solve output coefficients. These are directly relevant scientific-ML precedents, rather than merely applications of unrelated mathematics.

#### A guaranteed useful prediction application

Suppose a vector target y is known to satisfy a nonempty affine constraint set M. For any prediction \(\mu\), orthogonal projection obeys

\[
\boxed{\|\mu-y\|^2=\|\Pi_M\mu-y\|^2+\|\mu-\Pi_M\mu\|^2.}
\]

**Proof.** The correction is normal to M, while \(\Pi_M\mu-y\) is tangent. Expand the squared norm and the cross term vanishes. Thus enforcing a correct target constraint cannot worsen squared prediction error and improves it strictly when the original prediction violates the constraint.

This provides a real use case for conservation-constrained vector regression, compositional measurements and sensor reconstruction. It differs from arbitrary hidden constraints: the equality supplies information about the true target. It is established projection geometry, not a classification-accuracy theorem. If the supplied constraints are wrong, projection can increase error.

For a genuine joint Gaussian prediction \(N(\mu,\Sigma)\), with \(\Sigma\) positive definite and A full row rank, equality conditioning gives

\[
\mu_c=\mu-\Sigma A^T(A\Sigma A^T)^{-1}(A\mu-b),\qquad
\Sigma_c=\Sigma-\Sigma A^T(A\Sigma A^T)^{-1}A\Sigma.
\]

This is a possible integration with tabular foundation models. Separate scalar predictive distributions do not provide a calibrated joint covariance automatically. With uncertain constraints, a noise model should replace hard conditioning. The Euclidean nonincrease theorem above concerns orthogonal projection; a weighted correction instead has the corresponding weighted-metric guarantee.

The first experiment should compare unmodified prediction, ordinary QR correction, nullspace prediction and uncertainty-aware conditioning on tasks with independently justified constraints. Measure squared error, calibration, feasibility, incorrect-constraint sensitivity and total cost. An improvement shared with ordinary QR is a successful application of constraints, but not evidence that bias derivatives supplied the improvement.

#### Geometry inside a TabPFN style model

TabPFN learns an inference procedure from synthetic tasks. A plausible research route is to change those tasks and the information available during inference. The [official repository](https://github.com/PriorLabs/TabPFN) currently defaults to TabPFN-3.5; the [extensions](https://github.com/PriorLabs/tabpfn-extensions) already include embeddings, outlier detection, generation and imputation. These capabilities must be controls rather than claimed first applications.

Consider a task prior

\[
x=g_\omega(z)+\epsilon,\qquad
r_\omega(g_\omega(z))=0,\qquad y=h_\omega(z).
\]

Vary codimension, curvature, orientation, disconnected regimes, measurement noise, missingness and the predictive mechanism. A transformer could infer a task-specific manifold and use normal distances, tangent coordinates or derivative summaries as context. This differs from adding a fixed projection to a final head.

There is an exact representation rule for affine constraints. For full-row-rank A define

\[
P_N=A^T(AA^T)^{-1}A,\qquad q=A^T(AA^T)^{-1}b.
\]

The pair \((P_N,q)\) determines M by \(P_Nx=q\) and is unchanged by \((A,b)\mapsto(SA,Sb)\) for invertible S. Conversely, the same nonempty affine set has the same normal projector and minimum-norm anchor, so this pair is a complete invariant of that set in fixed Euclidean coordinates. This is established linear algebra. Using these quantities as task context could prevent sensitivity to arbitrary rescaling or recombination of the same equations. It does not provide invariance to arbitrary changes of input units; those require an explicit metric. A dense projector costs quadratic storage, so a scalable model needs an appropriate factorization or invariant contractions.

**Hypothesis:** a prior over noisy geometric mechanisms, with equation-invariant context, improves sample efficiency and robustness on related unseen tasks. Compare the same architecture and training budget with: the same synthetic tasks without geometric context; ordinary prior tasks; ordinary AD computing identical context; and current TabPFN with feature engineering. Hold out entire geometric families, not only samples from seen generators. If the same prior without derivative features gets the same gain, attribute the result to the prior.

Learning a full PFN is an expensive later stage. First test a constrained output adapter and a small task-conditioned model. Affine correction needs no bias derivatives; nonlinear jet extraction is where omnibias could supply a measurable implementation contribution.

#### Manifold learning clustering and anomaly detection

Let \(r_\theta(x)\in\mathbb R^m\) define a regular learned zero set with full-row-rank Jacobian J. The score

\[
s_\perp(x)=r_\theta(x)^T(JJ^T)^{-1}r_\theta(x)
\]

is exact squared distance for affine residuals and a local approximation for curved ones. On the manifold,

\[
P_T=I-J^T(JJ^T)^{-1}J
\]

gives tangent directions. Second derivatives provide curvature. Derive these quantities from one field; independent normal and Hessian outputs need compatibility checks.

**Hypothesis:** coherent curvature and normal geometry help distinguish touching manifolds or detect faults that move across a normal operating manifold. Useful stress cases include equal tangent planes with different curvature, intersecting operating regimes, small normal faults and large tangent displacements. A residual that learns to be identically zero is a degenerate solution, so reconstruction or contrastive information and rank controls are necessary.

A distance-only anomaly score misses rare points that lie on the manifold. It needs a density model along the manifold and a noise scale in the normal directions. Multiple charts also need regime probabilities and overlap handling. A sum of convenient scores should not be advertised as a normalized likelihood without deriving its change-of-variables and volume factors.

Existing methods include the [Manifold Tangent Classifier](https://proceedings.neurips.cc/paper_files/paper/2011/hash/d1f44e2f09dc172978a4d3151d11d63e-Abstract.html), [Deep SVDD](https://proceedings.mlr.press/v80/ruff18a.html), [DROCC](https://proceedings.mlr.press/v119/goyal20c.html), and [Neural Manifold Clustering and Embedding](https://arxiv.org/abs/2201.10000). Compare local PCA and mixtures of probabilistic PCA as well as learned methods. Measure anomaly recall at fixed false-positive rates, clustering quality, calibration, rank failures and full derivative cost. Compare identical fields evaluated with ordinary AD and omnibias; representation gains and derivative-engine gains are separate findings.

The existing consumer `omnibias-geometry` already contains learned-chart metrics, tangent/normal projectors and curvature machinery. Reuse it. The next research contribution would need a specific training rule, reliable geometric certificate or measured cost/accuracy gain beyond these controls.

#### Exact equality on Boolean data

The measure-zero objection for continuous inputs does not apply to the Boolean cube. The equality

\[
E_k(x)=\mathbf1\left\{\sum_{i=1}^n x_i=k\right\}
\]

selects an entire Hamming-weight class. In particular, \(E_1(x_1,x_2)\) is XOR.

There is a direct finite bias-stencil construction:

\[
\boxed{\tau(z)=\operatorname{ReLU}(z+1)-2\operatorname{ReLU}(z)
+\operatorname{ReLU}(z-1)=\max(0,1-|z|).}
\]

Therefore \(\tau(z)=\mathbf1\{z=0\}\) for every **integer** z. The proof follows by evaluating its four linear pieces and their endpoints. Affine residuals with integer weights and integer threshold/bias thus have an exact three-ReLU equality realization on Boolean inputs. On real noninteger inputs it is a tent, not an equality detector. Integrality, or a separately proved gap between zero and other attainable residuals, is essential. Learning unrestricted real weights does not preserve that condition.

This classical B-spline identity gives a concrete model candidate: small trainable counting blocks, with an exact hard implementation and a well-defined smooth expectation during training. For independent Bernoulli inputs,

\[
F_k(p)=\mathbb E[E_k(X)]=[t^k]\prod_i(1-p_i+p_it),
\]

\[
\partial_i F_k=\Pr(S_{-i}=k-1)-\Pr(S_{-i}=k).
\]

**Proof.** Condition on \(X_i\); the expectation is affine in \(p_i\). A count dynamic program evaluates a specified k in \(O(n(k+1))\) arithmetic operations. Every symmetric Boolean function has the representation \(\sum_{k=0}^n a_k E_k(x)\), using n+1 count-response entries instead of an unrestricted \(2^n\)-entry LUT. That saving applies to symmetric functions; learning which inputs form a useful group remains part of the task.

The expectation is a differentiable function of probabilities. It does not assign an ordinary derivative to the hard equality predicate. Exact expected derivatives can also vanish: parity has zero first derivatives at the fully symmetric probabilities for n greater than one.

Cardinality inference is established; [Tarlow et al., 2012](https://proceedings.mlr.press/r10/tarlow12a.html) gives fast exact methods. A fair comparison includes an independent count DP, hard popcount plus lookup, optimized counting circuits, [DiffLogic](https://github.com/Felix-Petersen/difflogic), [convolutional DiffLogic](https://arxiv.org/abs/2411.04732), and [DiffLUT-Net](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.09254), submitted 8 September 2026 with learnable six-input LUT functions and connectivity. Charging a counting block as one free operation would hide its hardware cost.

**Hypothesis:** learned small-support counting blocks improve sample efficiency or synthesized area/latency on unknown-support cardinality tasks, while generic LUT blocks handle nonsymmetric interactions. Include noisy counting, parity, count intervals and deliberately nonsymmetric tasks. Report hard accuracy, sample efficiency, training cost, hardening gap, synthesized size and latency. A benefit confined to counting tasks is a useful scoped result.

##### A further calculus and discrete difference identity

For a sufficiently differentiable scalar profile, successive Boolean differences of a ridge are finite bias differences. Repeated use of the fundamental theorem of calculus gives

\[
\sum_{S\subseteq\{1,\ldots,k\}}(-1)^{k-|S|}
\phi\left(z+\sum_{i\in S}w_i\right)
=\left(\prod_{i=1}^k w_i\right)
\int_{[0,1]^k}\phi^{(k)}\left(z+\sum_iw_it_i\right)dt.
\]

This is an exact bridge between calculus and Boolean interactions. At finite spacing the integral matters; substituting one point derivative is generally wrong. It suggests derivative-based interaction diagnostics for structured ridge models. It does not remove the difficulty of general high-dimensional integration or arbitrary Boolean optimization.

##### Shared inputs require joint information

Local multilinear gates can lose the global independent-input expectation interpretation when branches reconverge:

\[
\operatorname{softXOR}(p,p)=2p(1-p),\qquad
\mathbb E[X\mathbin{\mathrm{xor}}X]=0.
\]

Likewise soft AND gives \(p^2\), while \(\mathbb E[X\land X]=p\). These are limitations of that probabilistic interpretation, not errors in a deliberately chosen vertex-exact relaxation. For distinct Bernoulli variables, the AND discrepancy is their covariance; for XOR it is twice the covariance. Propagating pairwise covariances alone does not in general close a deep circuit's moment equations.

A candidate is to detect shared inputs and evaluate selected small subcircuits exactly, with cardinality DP or truth-table contraction. A resource-bound certificate could track the remaining approximation. Compare [DeepProbLog](https://proceedings.neurips.cc/paper/2018/hash/dc5d637ed5e62c36ecb73b654b05ba2a-Abstract.html), [Scallop](https://github.com/scallop-lang/scallop), weighted model counting and Boolean-quotient simplification. Exact inference for unrestricted circuits remains hard; a tractable structural restriction is part of the proposed result.

#### Nonlinear PDEs can have finite nonlinear solution families

The failure of finite linear spaces to close under arbitrary nonlinear products does not forbid finite **nonlinear** solution manifolds. For \(\nu>0\), let

\[
v(x,t)=c_0+\sum_{k=1}^K e^{-\nu k^2t}
\bigl[a_k\cos(kx)+b_k\sin(kx)\bigr],
\quad c_0>\sum_k(|a_k|+|b_k|).
\]

Then \(v_t=\nu v_{xx}\) and \(v\ge\delta>0\) for \(t\ge0\). Set

\[
u=-2\nu v_x/v.
\]

Writing \(\ell=\log v\) gives \(\ell_t=\nu(\ell_{xx}+\ell_x^2)\). Differentiate once in x and substitute \(u=-2\nu\ell_x\) to obtain

\[
u_t+u u_x=\nu u_{xx}.
\]

Linear coefficient dynamics thus produce a nonlinear Burgers solution, with exact periodicity and an explicit denominator certificate. The represented initial data are restricted to those obtained from this positive finite heat family; the construction does not contain every Burgers solution. This is classical Cole–Hopf, and learned linearizing coordinates already appear in [Gin et al.](https://arxiv.org/abs/1911.02710).

A worthwhile compiler target is a nonlinear realization map accompanied by domain, boundary, derivative-compatibility and error-transfer obligations. Its control must include the direct transformed spectral solver. A more general certified transformation, a new closure class, or better adaptive representation could be a result; reproducing Cole–Hopf alone is not one.

#### Optimization and large geometric models

For related LP instances, a neural model could propose an active set, followed by a linear solve and primal/dual feasibility checks. A valid optimality certificate can accept a correct proposal; otherwise a conventional solver supplies a fallback. Measure proposal cost, certificate cost, fallback frequency and total solve time against HiGHS with appropriate warm starts. Encoding constraints as hyperplanes does not discover the active set or remove Boolean integrality. Weighted cardinality with unrestricted integer weights also recovers subset-sum structure; bounded-weight DP is pseudopolynomial.

For a large geometric model, specify the task: reconstruct shapes, predict physical fields on shapes, or infer constraint systems. These need different data and architectures. [LaGeM](https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.01295) already studies large generative geometric models; [GATr](https://proceedings.neurips.cc/paper_files/paper/2023/hash/6f6dd92b03ff9be7468a6104611c9187-Abstract-Conference.html) provides an equivariant geometric transformer. Neural zero-set geometry and derivative-based shape learning also appear in [IGR](https://proceedings.mlr.press/v119/gropp20a.html) and [Exploring Differential Geometry in Neural Implicits](https://arxiv.org/abs/2201.09263).

An omnibias contribution could be a decoder producing one field with coherent values, normals and curvatures, plus checked local regularity and supported constraints. The proposed gain is reliable constrained adaptation or cheaper high-order evaluation at matched error. Large-scale pretraining is premature until this decoder has an advantage over ordinary implicit fields and the same derivative algebra.

#### Recommended research sequence

| Priority | Question | Evidence required to continue |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | Do equality/counting blocks help Boolean learning? | Gains against identical DP and current logic/LUT models at matched hard accuracy and hardware cost |
| 2 | Can true output constraints improve tabular predictions reliably? | Target-relevant constraints, calibrated uncertainty and robustness to constraint error; distinguish ordinary projection gains |
| 3 | Do coherent curvature features help manifold faults or clustering? | Gains over local geometry and learned controls at matched false-positive rate and total cost |
| 4 | Can a geometric PFN prior transfer beyond its synthetic generators? | Held-out mechanism families, matched priors/architectures, current TabPFN controls and a clear role for derivatives |
| 5 | Can a compiler certify nonlinear PDE realizations or continuous-parameter dictionaries? | A complete restricted theorem and comparison to the direct transformed solver or identical optimization algebra |

These are proposed studies, not results from the four-hour pilot. No blanket conclusion about all omnibias projects follows from the fixed-projection experiment. The strongest theory targets are a precisely stated representational separation, a stability/sample-complexity theorem under explicit assumptions, or a new tractable certificate. The strongest engineering targets are a measurable advantage in a defined task and a useful implementation of a guarantee that users can independently check.

This is the complete source note at compilation time. Its original experiment date, protocol, limitations and historical status apply; later corrections in the overview and subsequent audit notes take precedence. Heading levels, line endings, outer document spacing and source-relative Markdown links are normalized here; code and mathematical expressions are preserved.

### Calculus–geometry campaign: mathematics and evidence

This report accompanies the bounded research campaign of 19 October 2026. The
experiment implementations belong to the adjacent `omnibias-lab` consumer.
The [earlier pilot](/home/vardan/dev/projects/omnibias/docs/calculus-geometry-results.md) remains a separate, frozen
experiment. The constructions below preserve exact equality as a hard readout;
their training derivatives belong to a specified smooth computation.

The strongest result is a working **verified physical-calibration prototype**:
global field bounds, physical sensitivity enclosures and a proved finite loss
decrease on a fixed parameter interval. A separately derived energy certificate
also succeeds on a candidate for which the old contraction gate is provably
blocked. Its foundation is classical monotone-operator theory; the contribution
demonstrated here is the checked computational capability.

Correct output constraints reduced public TabPFN-v2 synthetic regression error
by **11.45% on five fresh confirmation seeds**, using ordinary QR projection.
The primary adaptive-speed and Boolean-learning candidates did not meet their
registered promotion gates. These findings support focused continuation in
verified calibration and constraint-aware prediction; they do not establish a
general theory or collapse-specific advantage. Section 5 retains all controls,
missed targets, setup limitations and replay results.

#### 1. The maps and their obligations

Write a neural realization, its jet, and its residual as

\[
\theta\xrightarrow{R}u_\theta
\xrightarrow{j^q}(u_\theta,Du_\theta,\ldots,D^qu_\theta)
\xrightarrow{C}(\mathcal N[u_\theta],\mathcal B[u_\theta]).
\]

The zero set of the last map describes represented solutions. A transformation
of coordinates is useful only when its effect on these maps is established.
The following propositions are established mathematics, with proofs included
to make the computational contracts explicit.

An arbitrary assignment of derivative coordinates is often called a formal
jet; one obtained by differentiating a single field is holonomic. A PDE
constrains jet coordinates, while compatibility constrains which coordinate
assignments come from a field. These are distinct requirements. The useful
compiler contract is to preserve both, together with boundary information.

##### Affine geometry and target constraints

Let \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) have full row rank and
\(M=\{x:Ax=b\}\). The minimum-distance problem has Lagrangian
\(\tfrac12\|y-x\|^2+\lambda^T(Ay-b)\). Stationarity gives
\(y=x-A^T\lambda\), and feasibility gives
\(AA^T\lambda=Ax-b\). Consequently

\[
\Pi_Mx=x-A^T(AA^T)^{-1}(Ax-b),\quad
L_M(x)=\tfrac12\|x-\Pi_Mx\|^2,
\]
\[
\nabla L_M=x-\Pi_Mx,\qquad
D\Pi_M=I-A^T(AA^T)^{-1}A.
\]

For reduced QR \(A^T=QR\), compute the correction as
\(Q R^{-T}(Ax-b)\). This uses a triangular solve and never forms a Gram
inverse. Numerical rank checks and numerical feasibility are distinct from
exact rational membership.

A linear system can also be differentiated with respect to its parameters.
For a nonsingular square system \(A(\theta)x(\theta)=b(\theta)\),
\(dx=A^{-1}(db-(dA)x)\). Linearity in the unknown does not make these
parameter derivatives zero. For an underdetermined system the derivative also
depends on the selection rule; the affine projection retains the starting
point's tangent component.

If the true vector target \(y\in M\), orthogonality proves

\[
\|\mu-y\|^2=\|\Pi_M\mu-y\|^2+\|\mu-\Pi_M\mu\|^2.
\]

Thus a correct affine constraint cannot increase squared prediction error.
This is an application guarantee, independent of a derivative engine. If the
target is \((0,0)\) and a wrong constraint forces its coordinates to sum to one,
projection produces \((1/2,1/2)\), increasing coordinate-mean squared error to
\(1/4\). There is no corresponding unconditional classification theorem.

The normal projector and minimum-norm anchor

\[
P_N=QQ^T,\qquad q=QR^{-T}b
\]

are unchanged under \((A,b)\mapsto(SA,Sb)\) for invertible \(S\).
They specify the same affine set by \(P_Nx=q\), and hence are a complete
invariant of a nonempty affine set in a fixed Euclidean coordinate system.
Changing measurement units requires an explicit metric. Supplying this context
to a PFN supplies task information; it does not demonstrate that the PFN
inferred the constraints.

##### Nonlinear roots, iteration maps and nearest points

For a regular residual \(r(y,\theta)\), the least-norm solution of
\(J(y)\delta=-r(y)\) is a correction to the *linearization*. Iterating these
corrections defines an iteration map whose derivative includes its dependence
on the seed. A root alone supplies no selection rule on an underdetermined
solution manifold.

A nearest-point branch instead satisfies the augmented equations

\[
y-x+J(y,\theta)^T\lambda=0,\qquad r(y,\theta)=0.
\]

Its differential is determined by

\[
\begin{bmatrix}
I+\sum_i\lambda_i\nabla_y^2r_i&J^T\\J&0
\end{bmatrix}
\begin{bmatrix}dy\\d\lambda\end{bmatrix}
=
\begin{bmatrix}dx-\partial_\theta(J^T)\lambda\,d\theta\\
-\partial_\theta r\,d\theta\end{bmatrix}.
\]

LICQ and a positive definite reduced Hessian make this bordered matrix
nonsingular and select a local stationary minimum branch. Calling it the
nearest point additionally requires the chosen neighborhood to have a unique
nearest point, or a justified global selection. Omitting the curvature term
changes the derivative. On a circle, a tangent-plane correction and radial
nearest projection already differ away from the circle.

##### Exact transfers between coefficient systems and PDEs

Let \(T:C\to V\) be linear and satisfy \(\mathcal LT=TM\). If
\(f=Tg\), then \(Mc=g\) implies \(\mathcal L(Tc)=f\). Boundary conditions
must also transfer: solve \((\mathcal BT)c=h\). This gives all solutions in
the represented family only when the coefficient equations correctly account
for \(\ker T\); an injective realization avoids that ambiguity. It gives every
PDE solution only if the representation contains every admissible solution,
which the finite pilots do not claim.

For nonlinear evolution \(u_t=\mathcal N(u)\), a differentiable realization
\(u=T(c)\) transfers coefficient dynamics \(\dot c=F(c)\) whenever

\[
DT(c)F(c)=\mathcal N(T(c)).
\]

The proof is the chain rule along the coefficient trajectory. Initial data,
boundary conditions, existence intervals and the domain of \(T\) remain
obligations. Finite linear polynomial families generally fail nonlinear
closure: squaring a nonzero quadratic generates a fourth-degree term.

For the concrete nonlinear example, take \(\nu>0\) and

\[
v=c_0+\sum_{k=1}^K e^{-\nu k^2t}
[a_k\cos kx+b_k\sin kx],\qquad
c_0>\sum_k(|a_k|+|b_k|).
\]

Then \(v\ge\delta>0\) for \(t\ge0\), \(v_t=\nu v_{xx}\), and
\(u=-2\nu v_x/v\) satisfies \(u_t+uu_x=\nu u_{xx}\). To prove it, put
\(\ell=\log v\), use
\(\ell_t=\nu(\ell_{xx}+\ell_x^2)\), and differentiate once in space.
This is the classical Cole–Hopf map, with exact periodic boundaries and a
restricted initial-data family. The direct transformed spectral solver is the
same mathematical control.

#### 2. Certificates for geometric transformations

##### Derivative compatibility

Suppose all proposed jet components \(J_\alpha\), including \(J_0\), are
polynomials. The finite conditions

\[
\partial_iJ_\alpha=J_{\alpha+e_i}\quad (|\alpha|<q)
\]

are necessary and sufficient for the entire jet to equal \(j^qJ_0\).
Necessity follows from differentiation; sufficiency follows by induction on
\(|\alpha|\). Checking equality of every coefficient is a computable exact
certificate. Polynomial PDE and boundary conditions add finite coefficient
equations. A correction in coefficient space can therefore retain one genuine
field; the certificate covers the chosen polynomial family.

Without a supplied value component, curl-free first derivatives yield a
potential on a simply connected domain, up to an additive constant. Topology
matters: \((-y/(x^2+y^2),x/(x^2+y^2))\) has zero curl on the punctured plane
but integrates to \(2\pi\) around the unit circle. Pointwise equation
constraints alone are insufficient: proposed derivatives \(p_x=0,p_y=x\)
violate mixed-partial compatibility.

There is also an explicit reconstruction map, rather than only a test. On a
domain star-shaped about zero, for a closed vector field \(p\), define

\[
T(p)(x)=u_0+\int_0^1p(tx)\mathbin{\cdot}x\,dt.
\]

To prove \(\partial_kT(p)=p_k\), differentiate the integral and use
\(\partial_kp_i=\partial_ip_k\). Its integrand becomes
\(p_k(tx)+t\sum_i x_i\partial_ip_k(tx)
=\tfrac{d}{dt}[t p_k(tx)]\). Integrating proves the claim. For a monomial
\(p_i(x)=c x^\alpha\), the contribution is exactly
\(c x^{\alpha+e_i}/(|\alpha|+1)\). Polynomial reconstruction therefore uses
only rational linear algebra.

The additional Python prototype projects two degree-two derivative polynomials
onto their three curl constraints, then reconstructs a degree-three potential.
For the incompatible proposal \((0,x)\), it returns \((y/2,x/2)\) and
\(u=xy/2\). Exact symbolic identities verify \(\Delta u=0\) on the square
and its prescribed boundary values on all four edges. The maximum principle
then gives uniqueness among classical solutions for these boundary data.
This corrects the derivative field and derives the value field; it does not
preserve an independently supplied incompatible value field. The projection
uses a Euclidean coefficient metric, with no assertion that this is the nearest
field in a physical norm. This is the polynomial Poincaré construction;
[finite element exterior calculus](https://arxiv.org/abs/0906.4325) provides a
much broader established theory of compatible differential spaces and
projections.

Even valid observed jets do not establish generalization. For finitely many
observations \(x_i\), adding
\(C\prod_i(x-x_i)^{q+1}\) preserves derivatives through order \(q\) at every
observation while changing the field elsewhere. A well-posed PDE with complete
boundary/initial data can add information that these jets do not contain.

##### Bias-cluster compression

For a common direction \(w\), write

\[
u(x)=\sum_j a_j\sigma(w^Tx+b+\epsilon_j),\quad
v(x)=\sum_{k=0}^p m_k\sigma^{(k)}(w^Tx+b),\quad
m_k=\frac{\sum_j a_j\epsilon_j^k}{k!}.
\]

Taylor's theorem applied to \(\sigma^{(|\alpha|)}\) gives

\[
\|D^\alpha(u-v)\|_\infty\le
|w^\alpha|\frac{\sum_j|a_j||\epsilon_j|^{p+1}}{(p+1)!}
\sup_I|\sigma^{(p+|\alpha|+1)}|=:e_\alpha,
\]

provided the entire segments between each shifted argument and the central
argument lie in \(I\). The interval fixture explicitly checks this domain.
It compares direct evaluation, derivative features and an 80-digit Newton
divided-difference reference. Different precision precludes a speed conclusion.

For a boundary cage \(g\), the derivative error transfers by Leibniz:
\(\|D^k[g(u-v)]\|\le\sum_{j=0}^k {k\choose j}
\|D^{k-j}g\|e_j\). Structural clamped boundary conditions are preserved.
For \(R(u)=u''''+\lambda u^3-f\) and \(\|u\|\le B\),

\[
\|R(v)-R(u)\|\le e_4+
|\lambda|(3B^2e_0+3Be_0^2+e_0^3).
\]

If a validated solution lies within \(\rho\) of \(u\), it lies within
\(\rho+e_0\) of \(v\). Meeting the original tolerance requires the error
budget to accommodate this increase, or a fresh residual certificate for \(v\).
These statements do not preserve parameter or selected-solution sensitivities
automatically; those require derivative bounds on the transformation and a
conditioned implicit solution map.

##### A constructive physical-sensitivity certificate

For the clamped problem \(u''''+\lambda u^3=384\), suppose a field certificate
proves \(\|u-v\|_\infty\le\delta\). Let \(B\) bound both fields and
\(M=1/384\) be the clamped Green-operator norm. If
\(\kappa=3|\lambda|B^2M<1\), Neumann inversion gives

\[
\|L_u^{-1}\|_{\infty\to\infty}\le R=\frac{M}{1-\kappa},
\qquad L_u=D^4+3\lambda u^2.
\]

The implicit function theorem then gives the physical sensitivity
\(L_u u_\lambda=-u^3\), with homogeneous clamped boundary data. For any
clamped sensitivity surrogate \(s\), enclose

\[
\eta\ge\|s''''+3\lambda v^2s+v^3\|_\infty,\qquad
S\ge\|s\|_\infty.
\]

Subtracting this equation from the true variational equation and using
\(|u^2-v^2|\le2B\delta\) and \(|u^3-v^3|\le3B^2\delta\) proves

\[
\boxed{\|u_\lambda-s\|_\infty\le
R\,[\eta+6|\lambda|B\delta S+3B^2\delta].}
\]

Every quantity on the right is computable from whole-domain enclosures. The
prototype fits a separate sensitivity readout by linear least squares, snaps
it to rational parameters, and checks its variational residual independently.
It does not identify the derivative of the network fitting procedure with the
physical solution derivative. At an observation \(x_0\), the intervals
\(u(x_0)\in v(x_0)+[-\delta,\delta]\) and
\(u_\lambda(x_0)\in s(x_0)+[-E,E]\) enclose the calibration gradient
\((u(x_0)-y)u_\lambda(x_0)\). Excluding zero certifies its sign at the stated
parameter. A finite optimization step requires additional neighborhood control.
This is an application of standard a posteriori residual and inverse bounds,
with an explicit scientific-learning use case.

For a finite step, repeat both enclosures on an entire parameter interval
\([a,b]\). If its calibration-gradient enclosure has upper endpoint
\(-\gamma<0\), the fundamental theorem of calculus proves
\(J(b)-J(a)\le-\gamma(b-a)<0\). A separate bounded follow-up tests the
fixed window \([32,33]\), with one frozen width-12 field, measurement \(9/10\)
and field radius \(1/100\). It must certify the whole window; a pointwise
gradient sign alone is insufficient.

##### A global monotone-energy alternative

For the clamped problem on \([0,1]\), a positive Green kernel gives a
stronger stability contract than the preceding contraction test. For
\(0\le x\le y\le1\), write

\[
G(x,y)=\frac{x^2(1-y)^2}{6}\,[3y-x(1+2y)],\qquad G(y,x)=G(x,y).
\]

It satisfies the clamped boundary conditions, is twice continuously
differentiable across the diagonal, and has unit jump in its third derivative.
The bracket is nonnegative because it is at least \(2y(1-y)\). Direct
integration and diagonal maximization give

\[
\sup_xG(x,x)=\frac1{192},\qquad
\int_0^1\!\int_0^1G(x,y)\,dx\,dy=\frac1{720}.
\]

Equip \(H^2_0(0,1)\) with energy norm \(\|z''\|_2\). Its evaluation
representer is \(G(x,\cdot)\), hence
\(\|z\|_\infty\le\|z''\|_2/\sqrt{192}\). To bound the one-norm,
let \(s=\operatorname{sign}z\). Green representation, Cauchy–Schwarz and
positivity give

\[
\|z\|_1=\langle s,z\rangle
\le\langle s,Gs\rangle^{1/2}\|z''\|_2
\le\frac{\|z''\|_2}{\sqrt{720}}.
\]

For \(z''''+q(x)z=f\) with clamped boundaries and bounded \(q\ge0\),
testing the weak equation with \(z\) yields

\[
\|z''\|_2^2+\int qz^2
\le\|f\|_\infty\|z\|_1,
\qquad
\boxed{\|z\|_\infty\le C\|f\|_\infty,
\quad C=\frac1{96\sqrt{15}}.}
\]

The zero-energy case is immediate; otherwise divide by \(\|z''\|_2\).
This proof does **not** assert positivity of the inverse of \(D^4+q\).
It uses positivity of the unperturbed one-dimensional Green kernel only.
General clamped biharmonic domains need not have that property.

For \(u''''+\lambda u^3=f\), \(\lambda\ge0\), existence and uniqueness
follow by minimizing the coercive, strictly convex energy
\(\frac12\int|u''|^2+\frac\lambda4\int u^4-\int fu\) on
\(H^2_0\). Weak lower semicontinuity and the one-dimensional Sobolev embedding
give a minimizer; its Euler equation and continuous \(f\) give a classical
\(C^4\) solution. For any clamped \(C^4\) candidate \(v\), subtracting
equations sets \(q=\lambda(u^2+uv+v^2)\ge0\). Therefore

\[
\boxed{\|u-v\|_\infty\le
C\|v''''+\lambda v^3-f\|_\infty.}
\]

No smallness assumption on \(\lambda\), the candidate amplitude or its error
radius is needed. A directed rational upper bound on \(C\), validated by
\(138240\,C_{\rm up}^2\ge1\), makes this a computable certificate when
paired with the existing whole-domain residual enclosure. The physical
sensitivity operator \(D^4+3\lambda u^2\) has the same inverse bound;
the earlier sensitivity proof may consequently replace its Neumann constant
with \(C\). Field approximation, residual enclosure and differentiating the
physical solution remain separate obligations.

This is an application of classical energy, Green-kernel and monotone-operator
arguments. [Dunninger and Locker (1975)](https://msp.org/pjm/1975/60-1/pjm-v60-n1-p05-p.pdf)
already establish existence and uniqueness for nonlinear monotone biharmonic
problems. [Grunau and Robert](https://arxiv.org/abs/0705.3301) explain the
limitations of positivity for general clamped domains. The explicit bound above
is proved here for this verification contract; a new mathematical principle
or optimal constant is not claimed.

##### Residual coordinates and a verifiable neighborhood

Let \(r(x,\theta)=0\) have a selected regular isolated solution and set
\(q(x,\theta)=S(x,\theta)r(x,\theta)\). If
\(\sigma_{\min}(S(x_*,\theta_*))=s>0\) and a proved variation bound is
\(\|S(x,\theta)-S_*\|\le L\rho<s\), then \(S\) is invertible throughout
that ball. Thus \(q=0\) and \(r=0\) have exactly the same zeros there.
At a root, \(q_x=S r_x\) and \(q_\theta=S r_\theta\); the terms multiplied
by \(r\) vanish. Therefore

\[
-q_x^{-1}q_\theta=-r_x^{-1}r_\theta.
\]

For constant \(S=r_x(x_*,\theta_*)^{-1}\), a bound
\(\|r_x(x,\theta_*)-r_x(x_*,\theta_*)\|\le L_J\rho\) gives
\(\|q_x-I\|\le\|S\|L_J\rho\). When this is \(\eta<1\),
\(\kappa_2(q_x)\le(1+\eta)/(1-\eta)\). This is classical local
preconditioning with an explicit sufficient neighborhood. Building and
applying \(S\) costs work; changing the metric can also change off-root
iterations. Preserving zeros does not preserve every training trajectory.

For a fully explicit nonlinear example, let
\(q_i(x,\theta)=x_i+x_i^2/4-\theta_i\),
\(r=\operatorname{diag}(10^{-6},1)q\), and
\(S=\operatorname{diag}(10^6,1)\). On \(\|x\|_\infty\le1/4\),
\(7/8\le\partial_iq_i\le9/8\), so
\(\kappa_2(q_x)\le9/7\). The scalar map sends the interval endpoints to
\(-15/64\) and \(17/64\), respectively; it is strictly increasing there.
Thus each \(\theta_i\in[-1/8,1/8]\) selects exactly one root in that box.
Both residual coordinates give the same sensitivity
\(\partial x_i/\partial\theta_i=(1+x_i/2)^{-1}\). The unscaled Jacobian is
ill-conditioned while the selected solution and its derivatives are unchanged.
This proves a concrete conditioning improvement with an explicit neighborhood;
it is classical residual scaling, rather than a new linearization principle.

#### 3. Equality, Boolean expectations and optimization

The exact equality gate is \(E(z)=\mathbf1\{z=0\}\). On integer residuals,

\[
\operatorname{ReLU}(z+1)-2\operatorname{ReLU}(z)+
\operatorname{ReLU}(z-1)=\max(0,1-|z|)=E(z).
\]

The four linear pieces prove the identity. At \(z=1/2\), the value is
\(1/2\), establishing the integrality restriction. Integer weights and bias,
or a proved attainable-residual gap with corresponding scaling, are essential.

For independent Bernoulli variables with probabilities \(p_j\), the count PMF
is the coefficient vector of \(\prod_j(1-p_j+p_jt)\). For response table
\(a_0,\ldots,a_m\),

\[
q=\mathbb E[a_S],\qquad
\partial_{p_j}q=\mathbb E[a_{S_{-j}+1}-a_{S_{-j}}].
\]

Conditioning on one variable proves the derivative. Enumerating all assignments
shows exact equality with a full LUT whose entries are tied by Hamming weight.
The campaign uses deterministic observed inputs and independently randomized
wire choices, which makes these conditional probabilities well-defined even
if the observed features are correlated. Hard argmax wires may duplicate;
replay evaluates their actual deterministic circuit. Marginal composition
does not in general retain global joint semantics: soft XOR of \((p,p)\)
is \(2p(1-p)\), whereas \(X\operatorname{xor}X=0\).

The optimized expected-accuracy objective is exactly
\(N^{-1}\sum_i[y_iq_i+(1-y_i)(1-q_i)]\) for that stochastic model. Its
derivative is not an ordinary derivative of the deterministic hard predicate.
Parity can have vanishing expected gradients at symmetric probabilities.

For one learned block, let \(p_j^*\) be the probability of its selected hard
wire and let \(e\) bound the largest response-table rounding error. Coupling
the stochastic block with the hard block gives the uniform bound

\[
\sup_{x\in\{0,1\}^d}|q(x)-h(x)|
\le 1-\left(\prod_j p_j^*\right)(1-e).
\]

**Proof.** All sampled wires equal their selected hard wires with probability
\(\prod_jp_j^*\). On that event the expected response differs from the hard
response by at most \(e\); on its complement the difference is at most one.
The argument is valid for every deterministic input, including duplicated
wires. Directed exponential and sigmoid enclosures plus rational arithmetic
can bound the right side for the exact real stochastic model defined by the
saved parameters. Floating framework evaluation is checked separately. This
is a classical coupling bound; it can be too loose to be useful and supplies
no ordinary derivative of the hard circuit.

If the right side is strictly below \(1/2\), thresholding the soft probability
at \(1/2\) gives exactly the hard decision on **every Boolean input**. A
post-training procedure scales both routing and response logits by a common
\(\beta\), doubles \(\beta\) until a directed enclosure is below \(10^{-3}\),
and otherwise refuses at its budget. Strictly positive routing gaps and
nonzero response logits ensure eventual convergence of this sufficient bound.
Ties can make it inconclusive. A second evaluator uses directed mpmath
expressions independently of the core interval wrappers. The hard model is
unchanged; this certifies approximation to that model, not its accuracy against
unknown labels.

The Boolean domain is essential here. A continuous function cannot uniformly
approximate a continuous-space equality indicator with error strictly below
\(1/2\) in a neighborhood containing the surface and arbitrarily close
off-surface points: continuity would force its limiting off-surface value to
equal its on-surface value. Exact membership remains a separate hard readout.
The finite-domain certificate does not replace that intended definition.

##### A concrete statistical reason to test counting units

For a *known* support of size \(m\), arbitrary hard symmetric Boolean
responses have \(2^{m+1}\) possibilities, compared with \(2^{2^m}\) for a
general LUT. If the support is unknown but consists of distinct inputs, the
counting hypothesis class has at most
\({d\choose m}2^{m+1}\) functions. Because the implemented decoder allows
duplicate wires, its correct upper bound is instead

\[
|\mathcal H_{\rm count}|\le {d+m-1\choose m}2^{m+1}.
\]

**Proof.** A count ignores wire order. There are
\({d+m-1\choose m}\) multisets of \(m\) wires from \(d\) inputs and
\(2^{m+1}\) binary response tables. Different descriptions may define the
same function, so this is an upper bound. For unrestricted LUTs the coarse
bound \(d^m2^{2^m}\) suffices. For a finite class and independent observations
with zero-one loss, a union bound applied to Hoeffding's inequality gives,
simultaneously with probability at least \(1-\delta\),

\[
|R(h)-\widehat R(h)|\le
\sqrt{\frac{\log(2|\mathcal H|/\delta)}{2N}}
\quad\text{for every }h\in\mathcal H.
\]

This classical argument supplies a scoped reason for a counting prior to help
with a structured target. It neither guarantees that gradient optimization
finds the best model nor favors counting on nonsymmetric targets. It also
explains why support recovery and an exhaustive small-instance control matter.
The hard class bound does not automatically extend to every stochastic soft
training model or to arbitrarily composed deep circuits.

Here \(R\) is ordinary classification risk. The experiment samples a finite
cube without replacement and also reports balanced accuracy; the displayed
bound supplies a capacity argument rather than a numerical confidence claim
for those reported pilot scores.

##### An exact bridge from derivatives to Boolean interactions

Repeated application of the fundamental theorem of calculus gives

\[
\sum_{S\subseteq[k]}(-1)^{k-|S|}
\phi\!\left(z+\sum_{i\in S}w_i\right)
=\left(\prod_iw_i\right)
\int_{[0,1]^k}\phi^{(k)}\!\left(z+\sum_iw_it_i\right)dt.
\]

For \(k=1\), this is the usual integral formula for a finite difference;
induction applies it once more in the next coordinate. Thus an interval bound
on \(\phi^{(k)}\) over the full argument interval certifies the size and,
when it excludes zero, the sign of this Boolean interaction. Replacing the
integral with a single derivative at finite spacing is generally incorrect.
This is a classical discrete-calculus identity with a useful implementation
contract: derivative enclosures can certify interaction restrictions without
pretending that general Boolean optimization has become easy.

For LPs \(\min c^Tx\) subject to \(Ax\le b\), a proposed basis \(I\)
provides the candidate equations \(A_Ix=b_I\) and
\(A_I^T\lambda_I=-c\). Exact primal feasibility, \(\lambda_I\ge0\),
stationarity and complementarity prove optimality by weak duality. Finding a
valid basis remains part of the algorithm. The experiment charges archive
construction, proposal, exact checks and conventional fallback.

For constant \(A\) and affine parameterized \(b,c\), a nonsingular basis gives
affine formulas for \(x(\theta)\) and \(\lambda_I(\theta)\). Strictly positive
inactive slacks and basis multipliers give a verifiable neighborhood preserving
the active set: in the infinity norm, take the minimum of each positive slack
or multiplier divided by the one-norm of its parameter derivative. A zero
denominator imposes no restriction. A zero margin refuses a positive-radius
claim. At a transition, a globally differentiable LP solution map need not
exist; quadratic regularization defines a different optimization problem.

For mixed value and first-derivative observations of
\(\psi_b(x)=(x-b)_+^2\), dual pricing is

\[
c(b)=\sum_i q_i^{(0)}(x_i-b)_+^2+
2\sum_jq_j^{(1)}(x_j-b)_+.
\]

It is a continuous piecewise quadratic in \(b\). Data knots, interval
endpoints and interior stationary points exhaust its absolute maximum.
Rational inputs permit exact pricing and a checked continuous-dictionary dual
bound. An independent checker reconstructs each quadratic from three exact
values. Second-derivative observations at knots require an additional
convention and are excluded. A moment certificate gives no error bound away
from the observed functionals.

The source review is targeted, not an exhaustive novelty search. A combination

Preserve the checked affine/jet primitives, certificate replayers, exact Boolean
oracles and this bounded experiment suite. Keep the broader prototypes as
research components whose status is explicit. No stable public API, license,
service or domain was changed by this campaign.

The strongest continuation is **verified physical parameter calibration** for
problems with a provable stability contract. This campaign now supplies a global
state bound, physical-sensitivity bounds and a fixed finite-step demonstration.
The next evidence gate is a matched-accuracy, end-to-end comparison with strong
collocation, validated-numerics and certified reduced-basis controls on a broader
parameter family, including enclosure and replay costs. A wider automatically
checkable stability/realization class would be a specific mathematical target.

**Constraint-aware prediction with independently justified constraints** is a
second practical direction. Test uncertain constraints and real multi-output
tasks before any PFN pretraining. The strongest unresolved transformation question
is when a computable certificate can preserve both the selected solution and
its sensitivities beyond the restricted families proved here.
For Boolean learning, the next useful question is robust unknown-support
recovery at larger input dimension and with noise, against algebraic,
combinatorial and current learned-logic controls. These are concrete research
questions; this pilot supplies no basis for promising their outcome.

### Verified physical calibration: evidence report

This bounded CPU study implements guaranteed scalar parameter-set recovery for the stated clamped nonlinear boundary-value problem. All measurements are synthetic, generated from separately certified reference solutions. It compares neural, spectral and local reduced-basis proposals under the same mathematical assurance. The earlier [calculus–geometry campaign](/home/vardan/dev/projects/omnibias/docs/calculus-geometry-campaign.md) is preserved separately.

The integrated matrix recorded 108/108 trials; the point-sensor matrix recorded 54/54. Discovery promotion gate: **NOT MET**. Full details and exact uncertainty are retained in the [machine-readable summary](/home/vardan/dev/projects/omnibias/docs/benchmarks/verified_physical_calibration.json).

The primary neural recipe certified **0/6 case/noise groups**, each requiring three successful repetitions. The fastest fully completed conventional recipe was **spectral / bisection**, at **3.06 seconds median cold cost**. The useful outcome is a replayable physical-parameter recovery contract and explicit identifiability/conditioning arguments. The registered evidence does not establish a neural competitive advantage.

#### Mathematical contract

The study assumes the one-dimensional boundary-value problem

\[
 u''''+\lambda u^3=384,\qquad
 u(0)=u'(0)=u(1)=u'(1)=0,\qquad0\le\lambda\le512.
\]

For each parameter, the strictly convex coercive functional
\(E_\lambda(u)=\tfrac12\int|u''|^2+\tfrac\lambda4\int u^4-384\int u\)
on \(H^2_0(0,1)\) has a unique minimizer. The direct method and the
one-dimensional Sobolev embedding give existence; strict convexity gives
uniqueness. Its Euler equation and regularity yield the classical solution.
It is nonzero because the forcing is nonzero.

The earlier [global energy proof](/home/vardan/dev/projects/omnibias/docs/calculus-geometry-campaign.md#a-global-monotone-energy-alternative)
gives, for any exactly clamped \(C^4\) candidate \(v\),

\[
 \|u-v\|_\infty\le C\|v''''+\lambda v^3-384\|_\infty,
 \qquad C=\frac1{96\sqrt{15}}.
\]

For completeness, the unperturbed clamped Green kernel is, for \(x\le y\),
\(G(x,y)=x^2(1-y)^2[3y-x(1+2y)]/6\), extended by symmetry.
The bracket is nonnegative because its minimum on \(0\le x\le y\)
is \(2y(1-y)\). Direct rational identities check the boundary conditions,
continuity through order two, unit third-derivative jump,
\(\max_xG(x,x)=1/192\), and \(\iint G=1/720\).
The reproducing-kernel inequality yields
\(\|e\|_\infty\le\|e''\|_2/\sqrt{192}\).
For \(f=\operatorname{sign}(e)\), Cauchy–Schwarz in the clamped energy
space and positivity of this unperturbed kernel give
\(\|e\|_1=\langle f,e\rangle\le\|e''\|_2
\sqrt{\langle f,(D^4)^{-1}f\rangle}\le\|e''\|_2/\sqrt{720}\).
Testing \(e''''+q e=-r\), \(q\ge0\), against \(e\) gives
\(\|e''\|_2^2\le\|r\|_\infty\|e\|_1\).
Combining the inequalities proves the displayed constant, including the
zero-error case by continuity. The same proof applies to nonnegative bounded
potentials without assuming positivity of their Green kernels.

The argument applies to the error equation with nonnegative potential
\(\lambda(u^2+uv+v^2)\). The inverse of
\(L_\lambda=D^4+3\lambda u^2\) has the same bound. The implementation
uses a rational upper bound verified by \(138240C_{up}^2\ge1\).
No positivity of the perturbed Green kernel is assumed. Parameter-interval
certificates enclose the residual for every coupling in the stated interval.

##### Identifiability from an integrated observation

Define the quartic-potential observable

\[
 H(\lambda)=\frac14\int_0^1u(x;\lambda)^4\,dx.
\]

The implicit function theorem applies because \(L_\lambda\) is coercive
and invertible. Derivatives at the prior boundary are interpreted one-sided. The physical sensitivity \(s=\partial_\lambda u\)
satisfies \(L_\lambda s=-u^3\) with homogeneous clamped boundaries.
Therefore

\[
 H'(\lambda)=-\langle u^3,L_\lambda^{-1}u^3\rangle<0.
\]

Strict negativity follows from positive definiteness and \(u^3\ne0\).
Thus \(H\) is continuous and strictly decreasing and has a unique inverse
on its attainable range. This is a deliberately chosen distributed observable.
The assumed measurement error bound is on the integral itself; it is not an
inferred error bound from an arbitrary sparse sampling of a noisy field.

Let \(I=\int u^4\). Cauchy–Schwarz in the \(L_\lambda\) energy inner
product gives

\[
 -H'(\lambda)\ge\frac{\langle u^3,u\rangle^2}{\langle u,L_\lambda u\rangle}
 =\frac{I^2}{384\int u+2\lambda I}.
\]

The denominator identity follows by testing the original equation with \(u\).
It is strictly positive. A certified lower bound on \(I\) and upper bound on
the denominator therefore give a computable slope bound.

For a parameter bracket \([a,b]\), any certified observation witness at
\(q\ge b\) supplies \(I(\lambda)\ge4H(q)\). The energy estimate with
candidate zero gives the unconditional bound \(\|u\|_\infty\le B_0=C_{up}384\).
Consequently the implemented local bound

\[
 m_{[a,b]}=\frac{(4H(q)_{lo})^2}{384B_0+2bB_0^4}
 \le -H'(\lambda)\quad(\lambda\in[a,b])
\]

is sound whenever the numerator is positive. Every use records and replays
its right-hand witness. No empirical derivative estimate justifies exclusion.

##### State, quadrature and physical-sensitivity uncertainty

If \(\|u-v\|_\infty\le\delta\) and both fields have magnitude at most
\(B\), then

\[
 |H(u)-H(v)|\le B^3\delta.
\]

Polynomial candidate integrals are exact rational integrals. Neural candidate
integrals use midpoint Taylor quadrature: on a cell of width \(h\),

\[
 \int g=h g(c)+\frac{h^3}{24}g''(c)+R,
 \qquad R\in\frac{h^5}{1920}\,g^{(4)}([c-h/2,c+h/2]).
\]

Here \(g=v^4/4\); all derivatives belong to the same field. Directed interval
arithmetic encloses the remainder over the whole cell. Quadrature uncertainty
and state error are stored separately. A state target alone is insufficient
for an accurate observation and therefore cannot terminate the observation
refinement ladder.

For any clamped sensitivity candidate \(z\), let
\(\eta\ge\|z''''+3\lambda v^2z+v^3\|_\infty\) and
\(S\ge\|z\|_\infty\). Residual subtraction gives the independently
replayed physical-sensitivity bound

\[
 \|s-z\|_\infty\le C_{up}
 [\eta+6\lambda_{max}B\delta S+3B^2\delta].
\]

It concerns the physical solution map. The derivative of the numerical fitting
algorithm is a different object. Floating sensitivity approximations may propose
queries; only interval observations and proved slope bounds accept updates.

##### Recovering a complete parameter set

For observation interval \(Y=[y_-,y_+]\), monotonicity makes its feasible
preimage an interval, possibly empty or clipped at the prior boundaries. The
algorithm brackets the clipped inverse of each endpoint. A certified point
observation strictly above or below a threshold excludes the appropriate side.
When the threshold lies inside the observation enclosure, a valid slope bound
gives \(|\lambda_* - q|\le\max|H(q)-y|/m\). Rational outward rounding
preserves containment.

The outer feasible interval uses the outer endpoint brackets; an inner interval
is reported only where both inverse brackets prove membership. A separate
attainable-range test proves feasibility before the integrated recovery can be
`CERTIFIED`. Numerical endpoint uncertainty must total at most \(10^{-3}\)
in coordinates \(\lambda/512\). Measurement uncertainty can still leave a
wide physical parameter interval. Budget or precision exhaustion is
`INCONCLUSIVE`; it is never evidence that no solution exists.

Sparse sensors at \(1/4,1/2,3/4\) use complete parameter subdivision with
uniform field bounds. A cell is excluded only when one sensor range is disjoint
from its measurement interval. A cell is included only when all its ranges are
contained. All unresolved components remain. Replacing a parent requires two
valid children. `CERTIFIED` for this separate cover means that the unresolved
parameter width meets the tolerance; existence is reported separately and is
not inferred from a nonempty outer cover. Interior-sensor monotonicity is not
assumed. Reflection sends a solution to another solution with the same forcing
and clamped boundaries; uniqueness therefore proves u(x)=u(1-x). The quarter
and three-quarter sensors are redundant in this symmetric fixture. Three sensor
locations do not imply three independent pieces of information.

##### Two-parameter extension and its assumptions

For \(u''''+\lambda u^3=a\), \(a>0\), define

\[
 V(\lambda,a)=\min_u\left[\tfrac12\|u''\|_2^2+
 \tfrac\lambda4\int u^4-a\int u\right].
\]

The envelope theorem and implicit differentiation give

\[
 \nabla V=(\tfrac14\int u^4,-\int u),\qquad
 D^2V=-J^*L^{-1}J,\qquad J=[u^3,-1].
\]

The two columns are independent: if \(\alpha u^3-\beta=0\) everywhere,
continuity and the clamped endpoint give \(\beta=0\), and the nonzero field
then gives \(\alpha=0\). Hence the Hessian is strictly negative definite.
Integrating its quadratic form along the segment between two parameters proves
strict monotonicity of the gradient and global injectivity on a convex domain
with \(\lambda\ge0,a>0\). This establishes identifiability for this pair
of conjugate observables. It supplies neither a quantitative uniform conditioning
certificate nor an implemented two-dimensional recovery method.

The same calculation applies conditionally to a real Hilbert-space energy
\(E(u;\theta)=E_0(u)+\sum_i\theta_iF_i(u)\): assume a unique smooth
minimizer, a coercive invertible state Hessian \(L\), and twice continuously Fréchet-differentiable
functionals \(F_i\). Its conjugate observables \(O_i=F_i(u(\theta))\)
satisfy \(DO=-J^*L^{-1}J\), where \(J\eta=\sum_i\eta_iDF_i\).
This follows by differentiating state stationarity, then applying the chain
rule. Independent columns of \(J\) along a convex parameter domain give the
same injectivity proof. These are explicit sufficient conditions, not a claim
for arbitrary neural networks or PDEs. The envelope step is established theory;
see [Milgrom and Segal](https://milgrom.people.stanford.edu/wp-content/uploads/2002/03/Envelope-Theorems.pdf).
Computable quantitative conditioning and measurable observables remain separate
application requirements.

The assumptions matter. At zero forcing, \(u=0\) for every coupling, so coupling
is unidentifiable. A clamped-endpoint point sensor is likewise uninformative.
One scalar observable cannot generally identify two unknown parameters: locally,
\(H_\lambda\ne0\) permits a curve of \((\lambda,a)\) with the same
\(H\). For \(h(t)=(t-1/2)^2\) and exact measurement \(1/16\),
the squared observation loss vanishes at both \(t=1/4\) and \(t=3/4\).
Reducing that loss cannot distinguish the two parameters. These counterexamples prevent extending the recovery conclusion
to an arbitrary sensor, uncertain physics or an optimization trajectory alone.

A useful exact regularity counterexample is the clamped Green function
\(G(x,1/2)\). It is nonzero and piecewise cubic, with matching derivatives
through order two and a unit jump in its third derivative. Its fourth derivative
is zero inside each open cell but equals a Dirac load distributionally.
Ignoring the interface would therefore falsely certify the homogeneous problem.
The accepted witness types are global polynomials and analytic caged fields;
a SciPy spline cannot enter by supplying only its cell-interior derivatives.

#### Experimental protocol and cost accounting

Discovery uses couplings 24, 96 and 320 with seeds 1301, 1423 and 1543. Measurements carry certified reference uncertainty, with a separate bounded 0.1% uncertainty case. The reference is an independently fitted polynomial with 90-digit search and a 10^30 rational coefficient denominator; competing proposals use the fixed 10^12 denominator. Its whole-domain error certificate, not the floating collocation value, creates the observation interval. Generating parameters are absent from worker inputs.

Neural widths are 12 then 24, with 100 readout steps on seeded paired tanh features; the hidden weights and biases remain fixed. Conclusions about neural proposals apply to that recipe. Spectral controls use 7 then 12 Chebyshev modes and eight Newton steps. The local POD control uses seven fixed polynomial snapshots and energy-weighted SVD, retaining singular values above 1e-12 of the largest. It is not official pyMOR. SciPy is a numerical consistency comparator; CAPD, Arb and pyMOR were unavailable. No new comparator downloads were required.

Cold runs use isolated processes and include import/configuration, fitting, all accepted and rejected refinement attempts, certificate construction, serialization and replay. POD snapshot/basis setup is added to each cold calibration. Actual persistent-process batches charge shared initialization and family setup once. Their driver is selected on completed discovery recipes; confirmation freezes that choice. Persistent batches reuse a process warmed by correctness/control preparation; template caches are warm, while measured dependency-import/configuration startup and POD construction are charged once. The warm batches do not measure a fresh interpreter launch; cold calibrations separately charge the complete subprocess launch. Cold runs separately include fresh process and template initialization. Acquisition/reference-generation cost is common experimental fixture preparation, recorded separately from solving an inverse problem with supplied measurements.

The parent terminates each isolated calibration after 60 seconds. Measured cost includes input serialization and process termination overhead, so timeout rows may slightly exceed 60 seconds. Three repetitions are required for a completed case. Every candidate observation is replayed before it can exclude a parameter. Hard resource limits, precision floors and unavailable proofs remain explicit. Rows may report a resolved broad feasible interval when measurement uncertainty is large; outer width is never conflated with numerical endpoint uncertainty.

The additional full-campaign reproduction audit took approximately 1160 seconds from the recorded UTC boundaries. It repeats the already charged per-calibration field/decision replay and is recorded as an extra campaign audit, rather than silently adding a second assurance pass to one proposal family. Fixture preparation and every stage's measured duration are retained in the summary.

### Unifying representations, training geometry and verification

This 20 October 2026 audit revisits the user's objections to the preceding
calculus–geometry summary and the supplied 56-page multi-bias manuscript.
It adds independent checks, corrects two interpretations, and develops a
constructive framework. It does not establish that deep networks dominate every
learning algorithm or that the framework is mathematically new.

recorded in `inputs.json`. The relevant sections inspected are Appendix W,
