## Appendix 087: omnibias-lab/stability/README.md

Source: [omnibias-lab/stability/README.md](/home/vardan/dev/projects/omnibias_projects/omnibias-lab/stability/README.md). Original SHA256: `f093f94215a552ef190871de702c464de87cc00c56e9f0d1e15756fe6f10478c`.

This is the complete source note at compilation time. Its original experiment date, protocol, limitations and historical status apply; later corrections in the overview and subsequent audit notes take precedence. Heading levels, line endings, outer document spacing and source-relative Markdown links are normalized here; code and mathematical expressions are preserved.

### Tanh conditioning pilot

This is an unshipped numerical experiment. The change of basis is a classical
identity, not a new theorem about differentiation. All activation polynomial
coefficients come from `omnibias.core.verified.coeffs`; no backend owns another
coefficient recurrence. Explicit tanh derivative polynomial representations
are established mathematics; see
[Boyadzhiev, The Fibonacci Quarterly 45 (2007)](https://www.fq.math.ca/Papers1/45-4/quartboyadzhiev04_2007.pdf).

For the sigmoid derivative polynomial (P_n(s)), define (Q_n(r)) by the
exact integer change of variables

\[
Q_n(r)=(1+r)^{n+1}P_n\!\left(\frac{r}{1+r}\right).
\]

The implementation expands each shared integer coefficient using the binomial
theorem. For (n\ge1), (P_n(0)=P_n(1)=0), so (Q_n(r)=rA_n(-r)) with
degree at most (n). For (z>0), (r=e^{-2z}) and

\[
\tanh^{(n)}z=(-2)^{n+1}
\frac{r A_n(-r)}{(1+r)^{n+1}}.
\]

This follows by differentiating
\(\tanh z=1-2\sigma(-2z)\). Reflection uses
\(\tanh^{(n)}(-z)=(-1)^{n+1}\tanh^{(n)}(z)\).
The rational expression and the original monomial expression represent the
same real function, including at the fixed branch threshold `0.5`. There is
no mathematical kink introduced by choosing between these identities.

The three implementations expose different numerical tradeoffs:

| Path | Runtime transcendental evaluations | Limitation |
|---|---|---|
| `monomial` | One tanh | Cancellation of large polynomial terms near saturation |
| `eulerian_cached_tanh` | One tanh | Recovers (r=(1-|t|)/(1+|t|)) from rounded (t); lost tail information cannot be restored |
| `eulerian_exp` | One tanh and one exp | Preserves the exponential tail; costs another transcendental evaluation |

Both proposed paths retain the original polynomial at `|z|<=0.5`, chosen
before running the pilot. Each requested derivative costs linear Horner work
in its order after cached coefficient setup. Returning every derivative
through order (N) with this implementation costs quadratic total Horner
work; it is not the deep-network Riccati composition algorithm.

Run `uv run python -m stability.tanh_eulerian`. The artifact records orders
2, 4, 8, 16, and 32; both signs; the center; saturation through `|z|=40`;
and adjacent floating-point values around selected derivative roots.
Values are checked against independent `mpmath.diff` at 100 decimal digits.
Torch and JAX reverse gradients are checked against derivative order (n+1).
The fixed gate is absolute error at most `2e-12 + 2e-10*abs(reference)`
in **derivative units**. Timings include the actual proposed arithmetic;
JAX first-call compilation and warm calls are recorded separately.

The initial artifact contains 81 rows, including failures. The exp-tail
variant passes all 15 fixed-grid backend/order combinations, including
gradient checks where available. It still fails the strict value gate near
selected order-16 and order-32 derivative roots. The cached-tanh variant
also fails in deep saturation. These are useful limits, not grounds to
claim universal float64 accuracy. The artifact is diagnostic; it establishes
neither certified error bounds nor a general speed advantage.

At (z=20), binary64 tanh has rounded to one. A function of that rounded
value alone cannot distinguish it from other saturated inputs, whose exact
derivatives differ. In the pilot the cached-tanh order-32 value is zero,
while the true value is about `-3.65e-8`. The exp-tail path preserves it.
This is an information limit of the cached floating value, not a failure
of the real closed-form identity.

The next integration decision needs an explicit application accuracy
requirement, a conditioning/error indicator, higher-precision handling of
unresolved roots, and an end-to-end comparison against existing Riccati
composition and modern Taylor-mode implementations. No shipped omnibias
kernel is changed by this pilot.

## Appendix 088: omnibias-lab/tabular/DENSITY.md

Source: [omnibias-lab/tabular/DENSITY.md](/home/vardan/dev/projects/omnibias_projects/omnibias-lab/tabular/DENSITY.md). Original SHA256: `1591f6c67a8755369806af0c187c22619539f9a5c796f4f37a61ecabb8b7095c`.

This is the complete source note at compilation time. Its original experiment date, protocol, limitations and historical status apply; later corrections in the overview and subsequent audit notes take precedence. Heading levels, line endings, outer document spacing and source-relative Markdown links are normalized here; code and mathematical expressions are preserved.

### Frozen fitted-density geometry confirmation

This follows the training-only radial-score probe. All data draws below are
fresh and use five independent generation seeds: 4013,4021,4049,4057,4073.
The source, this note, inherited trainers, comparator lock and installed
versions are fingerprinted before collection. Results belong in a separate
report. No post-test changes to these algorithms or grids are allowed.

#### Question and precedents

Does a density fitted from unlabeled training observations yield a useful
low-dimensional representation and better fresh predictions? Do gains survive
an ordinary Gaussian profile supplied with exactly the same initialization?

This is an application of existing Stein-score dimension reduction, not a
new differentiable-decision mechanism. Close precedents include
[score features](https://arxiv.org/abs/1412.6514),
[non-Gaussian multiple-index estimation, NeurIPS 2017](https://papers.nips.cc/paper_files/paper/2017/hash/4db0f8b0fc895da263fd77fc8aecabe4-Abstract.html),
[generalized pHd](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jmva.2018.07.006), and
[generalized Stein SDR, August 2026](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.15121).
We do not reproduce the 2026 method: it estimates predictor scores by other
procedures and considers multivariate responses. Its first-order cross-moment
need not identify the symmetric scalar-label band-parity examples here.

#### Data

Six cases: Gaussian XOR16, Student-5 XOR16, Student-12 XOR16, elliptical
Student-5 XOR16, Gaussian XOR32 and Gaussian AND16. Training sizes are 4096
for D=16 and 8192 for D=32. Each has 1024 fresh validation and 4096 fresh test
observations. Five draws per case give thirty independently generated datasets.

For each draw a new orthonormal rank-two frame is generated. Symmetric bands
use the fixed Gaussian-median threshold 0.6744897501960817. XOR or AND combines
the bits, then 3% independent flips are applied. Student inputs have population
covariance I before an optional elliptical transformation; Student band bits
are not independent and need not each be balanced. The elliptical case applies
a random rotated mixing matrix with singular values geometrically spaced
from 0.5 to 2.5 and a nonzero random shift. The population covariance condition
number is 25. Planted directions enter only the generator and diagnostics.
No source density, degrees of freedom, mixing matrix, shift or normal is passed
to any learner. Rank two and the two-band rule grammar are supplied.

#### Estimated density and score matrices

Training rows are split into two seed-fixed halves. Each half fits its own
location and covariance, whitens its fitting observations and estimates the
radial density. These are then evaluated only on the other half. Both fold
matrices are mapped back into original coordinates and averaged with weights
proportional to the number of scoring observations. This prevents a density
fit from using the observations in its own score average. It does not make
the fitted score exactly unbiased or provide a finite-sample theorem.

Two density recipes use the same folding:

1. Gaussian radial density with its variance fitted by maximum likelihood.
2. Training BIC selection between that Gaussian and a spherical Student density
   with fitted degrees of freedom and variance. Student fitting uses three
   L-BFGS-B starts (nu=5,20,100), nu bounded to [2.1,200] and variance [0.1,10].
   Convergence, boundaries and likelihood/BIC values are recorded. Covariance
   is the preliminary empirical estimate, not a joint robust t-scatter MLE.

For p(z)=psi(r), r=||z||^2, second- and traced-fourth score matrices are
Hess(p)/p and Hess(Delta p)/p, each A(r)zz^T+B(r)I. `density_scores.py` gives
the Gaussian and general-Student coefficients. With a=(nu+d)/2,c=(nu-2)*v,

    A2=4a(a+1)/(c+r)^2; B2=-2a/(c+r)
    A4=8a(a+1)(a+2)*[(nu+2)r-(d+4)c]/(c+r)^4
    B4=4a(a+1)*[(d+2)c-(nu+2)r]/(c+r)^3.

Label signs 2y-1 weight their averages. Under a fold whitening z=(x-mu)T,
the matrix is mapped as T M_z T^T. The fourth trace is taken in the fold's
whitened coordinates, not by asserting Laplacian invariance to general affine
transformations. Independent density-autodiff oracles check the derivatives.

#### Comparators and selection

All predictors receive the same final training-mean/covariance whitening,
fixed on validation/test. Cross-fitted raw-coordinate score matrices are
converted into this predictor coordinate system before eigendecomposition.
Second/fourth score matrices select the two largest-magnitude eigenvalues;
SAVE and full Hermite U select the largest algebraic eigenvalues.

Seven subspaces: random, SAVE, full fourth-Hermite sign-label U, cross-fitted
Gaussian degree two/four, and fitted-density degree two/four. Full Hermite U
uses the same final training-whitened rows as its direct-rule/NN predictions.
Because that transformation is fitted on those rows, no iid unbiasedness is
claimed for this comparator. Each basis receives the inherited 24-partition
two-band rule learner. The adaptive fitted-density rule selects degree two
or four by validation log loss, with no extra fitted candidates.

Six ridge models combine collapsed sech-squared or ordinary Gaussian profiles
with random, adaptive fitted-density and full-U initialization. This closes
the previous study's omission of the stronger sign-label full-U initializer.
The profiles have matched FWHM and parameter counts, identical head seeds,
32 features and the same trainable normals/centers. Three learning rates
(0.001,0.003,0.01), at most 180 AdamW epochs, validation every five epochs and
ten-check patience follow the frozen inherited trainer. Estimated initializer
selection has additional validation search through the direct rules; both
profiles share that choice. No hidden directions or test data select it.

An ordinary 64/32 ReLU MLP, LightGBM (15/31/63 leaves) and CatBoost (depth
4/6/8) are additional controls, using their inherited three-trial settings.
Boosting has at most 500 iterations and 50-iteration validation early stopping.
This is not an exhaustive tabular benchmark. Earlier real-data and TabM studies
remain separate; this study makes no broad superiority claim over those methods.

There are 17 selected predictors per draw, or 510 test evaluations. Direct
rules fit 5040 candidate partitions in total. The six ridge models and three
other controls attempt 810 fits. Test log loss is primary; AUROC, accuracy and
F1 at fixed 0.5 are secondary. Tuning/compute differ between recipe families.
The five independent draws support a stronger descriptive check, not a claim
of global significance. Failures and warnings are retained. No speed, GPU,
memory, certification or novelty claim follows from this learning study.

#### Reproduction

Use the existing optional Python 3.12 comparison environment and
`tabular/requirements.lock`, rather than modifying the lab's Python 3.14 lock.

```bash
python -m pytest -p no:cacheprovider tests/test_density_scores.py tests/test_density_study.py -q
python -m tabular.density_study --output artifacts/density_study.json
```

Subsets use `--cases` and `--seeds`, and have distinct provenance. Resume
requires exactly matching source, protocol, command matrix, dependencies/lock
and generated arrays. A separate seed outside the matrix may smoke-test the
pipeline; it must not be pooled into the frozen results or used to tune the
main matrix. Resource refusals are errors, not missing favorable rows.

versus 0.6165/0.6330 with fitted radial scores. Correctly selecting the density
family does not guarantee that a partial trace is the best signal estimator.

#### Mathematical interpretation and limits

Score-based geometry has direct precedents in
[non-Gaussian multi-index learning (2017)](https://papers.nips.cc/paper_files/paper/2017/hash/4db0f8b0fc895da263fd77fc8aecabe4-Abstract.html),
[score features](https://arxiv.org/abs/1412.6514),
[elliptical pHd](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jmva.2018.07.006), and
[generalized Stein SDR (2026)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.15121).
This study does not reproduce the latter's particular estimator or claim the
general score mechanism as new. The separately derived band-parity population
coefficient shows how a second-order Student score can carry geometry whose
balanced Gaussian second-order score vanishes. It is an explicit worked case,
with novelty unchecked, not a new calculus or an LP complexity theorem.

Gaussian inputs have independent coordinates; Student coordinates share a
random radial scale and their band bits are dependent. The common fixed band
threshold also changes their marginal balance. The separate theoretical check
repeats the identity for per-law marginally balanced bands and still obtains
a nonzero Student coefficient. This study itself retains the original frozen
fixed-threshold data, rather than mixing in a post-outcome task change.

Both density and final predictor preprocessing are training estimates. The
full Hermite comparator uses the final training-whitened rows, so its usual
known-Gaussian iid unbiasedness is not asserted. Higher-order score noise,
unknown rank, nonelliptical data and general symbolic grammar remain outside
the demonstrated scope. No new-mathematics, hard-equality-gradient, generic
tabular, PDE, LP, certification or commercial-value claim follows.

python -m tabular.density_analysis --input artifacts/density_study.json --output artifacts/density_summary.json --report tabular/DENSITY_RESULTS.md
```

The separate smoke seed 9001 is not pooled with these results. Source/command,
dependencies/lock and every generated array are checked on resume. The summary
refuses incomplete, duplicated, altered-source or subset matrices. Raw outputs
stay in lab artifacts; the main repository snapshot normalizes machine paths
and is not a raw resume input. The 36 focused checks cover score derivatives,
fold separation, coordinate transforms, fresh generation, training-only
preprocessing, the explicit population coefficient and its Gaussian limit.

## Appendix 090: omnibias-lab/tabular/METRIC_EXPECTATION.md

Source: [omnibias-lab/tabular/METRIC_EXPECTATION.md](/home/vardan/dev/projects/omnibias_projects/omnibias-lab/tabular/METRIC_EXPECTATION.md). Original SHA256: `35c30c1fe6d10b5caa810aeda6d5de78cfb386ad449884b1213a296425252c27`.

This is the complete source note at compilation time. Its original experiment date, protocol, limitations and historical status apply; later corrections in the overview and subsequent audit notes take precedence. Heading levels, line endings, outer document spacing and source-relative Markdown links are normalized here; code and mathematical expressions are preserved.

### Exact expected F1, a variance enclosure and its limits

This is a mathematical and numerical reference, with no model-training or
speed claim. Known binary labels y are fixed; predictions Z_i are independent
Bernoulli(p_i). Empty-positive F1 is defined as zero. This convention differs
from papers taking 0/0 as one. The implementation is bounded to n<=1024.

#### Existing work and the current paper code

[Jansche (2007)](https://aclanthology.org/P07-1093/), Sections 1.3 and 3,
explicitly computes expected F-score under independent Bernoulli outputs and
discusses using it in smooth training. This predates omnibias and is more
specific than merely saying annealing is old. The paper's exact dynamic
program is different from the quadrature representation implemented here.
Neither exact metric expectation nor its smooth-training interpretation is
claimed as new. The primary PDF is preserved in `artifacts/sources/`.

The local temperature-collapse paper's `src/study.py:metric_loss` computes
the ratio 2*sum(y*p)/(sum(y)+sum(p)), plus regularization. That is soft F1.
Its `threshold` routine does validation tuning for the BCE baseline too;
we do not claim that baseline simply used a fixed 0.5 threshold. The existing
head-refinement results are separate from this audit, which fits no classifier.

#### A cheap two-sided bound

Let P=sum(y)>0, A=sum(y_i Z_i), K=sum(Z_i), a=E[A], mu=E[K], b=P+mu,
V=Var(K)=sum p_i(1-p_i), C=Cov(A,K)=sum y_i p_i(1-p_i), and S=2a/b.
With delta=K-mu, the exact reciprocal identity gives

\[
E[F1]=S-\frac{2C}{b^2}
+\frac{2}{b^2}E\left[\frac{A}{P+K}(K-\mu)^2\right].
\]

Indeed 1/(b+delta)=1/b-delta/b^2+delta^2/(b^2(b+delta)),
E[A*delta]=C, and E[delta^2]=V. Since 0<=A/(P+K)<=1/2, we obtain

\[
L=S-\frac{2C}{b^2}\le E[F1]\le
S+\frac{V-2C}{b^2}=U.
\]

These are smooth O(n) functions of the probabilities. Their midpoint is

\[
M=S+\frac{V/2-2C}{b^2},\qquad
|E[F1]-M|\le\frac{V}{2b^2}\le\frac{1}{8P}.
\]

The final inequality uses V<=mu and mu/(P+mu)^2<=1/(4P).
Similarly |E[F1]-S|<=2V/b^2<=1/(2P). Thus an expensive exact expectation
can have only a small *value* difference from the corrected proxy when P is
large. This is not a gradient-closeness, training-convergence or generalization
theorem. The midpoint is not guaranteed to be pointwise closer than soft F1.

For a fixed feasible model family and globally optimized M, its expected-F1
regret relative to a global expected-F1 optimizer is at most 1/(4P), by applying
the uniform value bound twice. This statement requires global optimization;
the neural training algorithms here do not establish it. The analogous soft-F1
bound is 1/P. No such statement identifies the hard deployed argmax metric.

`rational_bounds` performs this finite calculation with exact Fractions,
including exact conversion of supplied binary floats. It encloses the expected
metric for those exact probabilities, conditional on independence and the
proved inequalities. It does not enclose an upstream neural/sigmoid evaluation
or population risk, and it is not a formal proof build. `smooth_bounds` evaluates
the unclipped formulas with ordinary tensor arithmetic, preserving gradients;
its floating endpoints are not themselves outward-rounded certificates.

Examples show why the direction of bias matters. With y=(1,0), p=(1/2,1/2),
S=1/2 and exact E[F1]=5/12. With p=(1,1/2), S=4/5 and exact E[F1]=5/6.
Soft F1 is neither a universal upper nor a universal lower bound.

#### An algebraically exact quadrature representation

Using 1/(P+K)=integral_0^1 t^(P+K-1) dt and independence,

\[
E[F1]=2\int_0^1 t^P\sum_i y_ip_i
\prod_{j\ne i}(1-p_j+p_jt)\,dt.
\]

The integrand is a polynomial of degree at most P+n-1. Consequently
ceil((P+n)/2) Gauss-Legendre nodes integrate it exactly in exact arithmetic.
The log-product implementation is a finite differentiable tensor expression;
its floating evaluation and node generation are numerical approximations.
Complexity is O(n*(n+P)) in arithmetic/storage. This is an eager prototype,
with no JIT, GPU performance or arbitrary-order gradient claim.

An independent rational count-convolution reference and brute-force discrete
enumeration check values and probability derivatives for small cases. The
derivative identity is E[F1|Z_i=1]-E[F1|Z_i=0], an instance of the classical
multilinear extension. Parameter gradients through sigmoid logits are checked.

#### Frozen numerical audit

Sizes 2,8,32,128,512,1024; positive counts from 0,1,n//10,n//2,n; three fixed
seeds; uniform, beta, near-correct, perfect and half-probability inputs; both
float32/float64. Inputs are cast before an independent float64 count-convolution
oracle is computed, separating computation error from input quantization.
All 810 cases and every rational interval are preserved in JSON.

| Dtype | Cases | Failed gates | Max quadrature/reference error |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| float32 | 405 | 0 | 1.36e-05 |
| float64 | 405 | 0 | 3.23e-11 |

The native float32 worst case is a near-correct n=1024 vector with one positive.
The float64 worst case has all probabilities and labels one at n=1024.
The independent numerical comparison is not an enclosure of the quadrature.
No numerical-training benefit follows from these passing gates. All thirteen
focused checks pass, including exhaustive rational small cases, endpoint
conventions, gradients, dtype/resource refusals and permutation invariance.

#### The actual LP connection

For known y and a polytope Ap<=d, 0<=p<=1, maximizing S is a classical
linear-fractional program. Set s=1/(P+sum p), q=s*p. The equivalent LP is

    maximize 2*y^T*q
    subject to A*q <= d*s, 0<=q<=s, P*s+sum(q)=1.

This is [Charnes-Cooper (1962)](https://doi.org/10.1002/nav.3800090303).
Combining a verified LP upper bound on S with the value-gap inequality can
bound the optimum expected F1 on that specified feasible set. A floating
solver's reported optimum alone is not a verified LP bound. A replayable LP
certificate integration now exists separately in `metric_lp_bridge.py`, with a
76-case audit. The main bias/PDE research record documents its scope and gaps.

The expected metric itself need not be a linear-fractional function. For
y=(1,0), p1=9/10+t, p2=3t, 0<=t<=1/10, exact expected F1 is
9/10+t/10-t^2. Its maximum is at t=1/20 with value 361/400, while soft F1
is maximized at t=0. Even these linear constraints do not make the exact
expected metric the same LP. A neural parameterization p=sigmoid(Xw) also
imposes nonlinear feasibility constraints; the independent-p LP is then a
relaxation rather than an exact optimizer over neural weights.

The variance enclosure and this composition are worked deductions here.
Their novelty has not been established. A separate frozen small-positive study
now compares six objectives with threshold-tuned BCE and weighted BCE. Expected
F1 has no strictly higher case mean than BCE in that final-point recipe; it
does not yet test validation checkpoints or a no-update BCE fallback. See
`metric_learning_study.py` and the main bias/PDE research record for all trials
and limitations. Minibatch expected F1 generally differs from global expected F1;
neither this proof nor a numerical pass removes that issue.

python -m tabular.metric_expectation_report --input artifacts/metric_expectation_audit.json --output artifacts/metric_expectation_summary.json --report tabular/METRIC_EXPECTATION.md
```

Heading levels, line endings, outer document spacing and source-relative Markdown links are normalized here; code and mathematical expressions are preserved.

### Frozen same-matrix pair-kernel benchmark

This is a computation experiment, separate from the completed learning study.
It does not change the estimator, improve its statistical information, or
establish a new derivative method. The derivation uses classical Gaussian
Hermite generating-function algebra. Novelty has not been established.

For s=x.z and u=||x||^2+||z||^2, the normalized fourth-tensor unfolding product
G(x,z)=Phi4(x)Phi4(z)^T is

    24G = [s^3+3(d+6-u)s] xz^T
          -3[s^2+d+4-u](xx^T+zz^T)
          +6s zx^T+3[s^2+d+2-u]I.

One route is to differentiate the scalar fifth Hermite kernel in its two
arguments and subtract five times the fourth scalar kernel times I. The
Gaussian generating function supplies those scalar polynomials. This is a
closed expression for the same matrix, not a tensor approximation.

For symmetric sample-pair weights W, summing ordered pairs combines xz^T and
zx^T. The remaining terms use X^T A X, weighted xx^T sums and a scalar identity
term. Diagonal pair weights are set to zero for a U-statistic. The prototype
therefore needs O(n^2*d) arithmetic and O(block*n+d^2) working storage, excluding
inputs; it never constructs d^4 coefficients. This may lose when n is large
relative to d. It is not a theorem of improved time to accurate learning.

Two exact tensor controls are required. The first uses the previous blocked
quadratic-feature Gram reference. The stronger second stores only upper
triangular x_a*x_b features for the Gram, then reconstructs the symmetric mean
tensor with Wick corrections. The symmetry-compressed control supports d<=64;
the original reference retains its d<=32 refusal. Neither control forms one
fourth tensor per observation. The comparison uses the fastest available tensor
control for each row. Independent checks compare both controls and the pair
formula, including biased/unbiased averages, both label kernels, block sizes,
rotations, label swaps and arbitrary weighted means.

The frozen grid crosses dimensions 8,16,32,64 with n=256,2048, and sign/RBF
binary-label kernels: 16 rows. Inputs are float64 CPU arrays with one BLAS
thread. Each row uses nine distinct runtime input perturbations of size 1e-4,
two warmups per method and interleaved method order. All nine output matrices
are compared before timing summaries are accepted. The maximum relative
Frobenius discrepancy must be <=2e-10. Medians, minima, maxima and every timing
sample are retained; gains are not promoted where sample ranges overlap.

No inference about sample adequacy follows from this grid. In particular, a
matrix can be cheap to form when the observations are insufficient for recovery.
There is no GPU, compilation, gradient, memory-ratio or general speed claim.
Mixed-process RSS would not establish an operator memory ratio. Allocation and
array operations are included in warm timings; imports/input generation are
outside those kernel timings. Source, protocol, input/output digests, runtime
versions and the existing optional comparator lock are captured. This note is
hashed before timing collection and is not edited to describe results.

```bash
python -m pytest tests/test_hermite_pair_kernel.py -q
python -m tabular.pair_kernel_benchmark --output artifacts/pair_kernel_benchmark.json
```

Source/protocol/dependency changes refuse resume. A failed row remains a failure.
Results and limitations belong in a separate report.

## Appendix 092: omnibias-lab/tabular/PROFILES.md

Source: [omnibias-lab/tabular/PROFILES.md](/home/vardan/dev/projects/omnibias_projects/omnibias-lab/tabular/PROFILES.md). Original SHA256: `0b2db4148e110509e82952cb08de3af4346b240f72c5255b6dab99ae7825f130`.

This is the complete source note at compilation time. Its original experiment date, protocol, limitations and historical status apply; later corrections in the overview and subsequent audit notes take precedence. Heading levels, line endings, outer document spacing and source-relative Markdown links are normalized here; code and mathematical expressions are preserved.

### Frozen stronger-profile and projected-classifier comparison

The fitted-density study found a modest fixed-width sech-squared advantage.
This follow-up strengthens the shape and classifier controls before drawing
a mechanism claim. It uses entirely new generation seeds
5137,5153,5167,5189,5197; no previous test arrays are reused.
The six generators, data sizes, hidden rank, noise and elliptical transformation
are inherited unchanged from [the density protocol](/home/vardan/dev/projects/omnibias_projects/omnibias-lab/tabular/DENSITY.md). This note,
source, inherited code, dependency versions and comparator lock are hashed
before collection. Results belong in a separate report.

#### Shared geometry

All methods receive one common estimated plane. Full sign-label Hermite U and
fitted-density scores of degree two and four each seed the same 24-partition
direct-rule learner. Validation log loss chooses among those three bases.
A training-only fourth angular phase rotates the selected plane. The inherited
ridge initializer places the same 32 features within it. Planted directions,
input law and tail parameters are unavailable to fitting and selection. Rank
two and the symmetric two-band rule grammar are supplied.

There are six cases and five independent draws each. Each has 4096 training
rows in D=16, or 8192 in D=32, 1024 fresh validation and 4096 fresh test rows.
Training mean and covariance provide the common predictor whitening. The
cross-fitted density procedure uses original training rows. Input Student band
bits are dependent and not necessarily marginally balanced at the fixed
Gaussian-median threshold. This is a restricted synthetic study, not a claim
about arbitrary tabular data or symbolic discovery.

#### Matched bell functions and widths

All five profiles have value one at zero and half maximum at +/-h. With r=z/h:

| Profile | Function |
| --- | --- |
| Collapsed / logistic bell | sech^2(acosh(sqrt(2))*r) |
| Gaussian | exp(-log(2)*r^2) |
| Laplace | exp(-log(2)*abs(r)) |
| Cauchy | 1/(1+r^2) |
| Hyperbolic secant | sech(acosh(2)*r) |

The logistic bell is also a normalized ordinary logistic density; see
[SciPy's logistic distribution](https://docs.scipy.org/doc/scipy/reference/generated/scipy.stats.logistic.html).
This is not a new function merely because it has a collapse construction.
An independent ordinary-PyTorch realization is checked for values, gradients
and matched optimizer updates. Laplace has the conventional absolute-value
subgradient at its center. Stable log-space formulas avoid cosh overflow.

Two controls retain the exact earlier fixed-width collapsed and Gaussian
implementations. All five profiles also learn one width per feature. Initial
h=2*acosh(sqrt(2))/8 is shared. A raw parameter a maps to

    h(a)=h0*exp(log(16)*tanh(a/log(16))).

This smooth map bounds the width multiplier between 1/16 and 16 and has
unit derivative of log-width at a=0. All learned-profile models add exactly
32 parameters, use identical starting normals/centers, head seeds and
architecture, and learn the full-space normals, centers, widths and head.
The fixed profiles have 32 fewer trainable parameters. Half widths and
parameter counts are recorded for every trial.

All ridge models retain the raw-input skip and 32-unit ReLU head. Three
learning rates 0.001,0.003,0.01, at most 180 full-batch AdamW epochs,
checkpointing every five and ten-check patience follow the inherited trainer.
The same data, parameter seeds and validation selection apply to all profiles.

#### Independent models on the same plane

Four further controls operate directly on the two projected coordinates:
64/32 ReLU MLP, LightGBM, CatBoost and RBF SVM. The first three use their
inherited three-trial settings. Boosting has at most 500 iterations and
50-iteration early stopping. RBF SVM gets nine combinations C=1,10,100 and
gamma=0.25,1,4, probability=True, a 512 MiB cache and one million maximum
iterations. Its probabilities use training-only internal calibration.
Nonconvergence is a failed trial, never an accepted optimum. See the
[official SVC documentation](https://scikit-learn.org/stable/modules/generated/sklearn.svm.SVC.html).

The projection models cannot refine normals outside the fixed estimated
plane. Ridge models can, and they also retain the full raw-input skip. SVM
has more trials than the other classifiers. These unequal representations,+tuning and compute budgets are explicit; no global superiority claim follows.
The validation-selected direct rule itself is the twelfth selected predictor.

There are 360 planned test evaluations. Geometry selection considers 2160
rule partitions. The seven profile models, three projected neural/boosting
controls and SVM attempt 1170 fits in total. Test log loss is primary;
accuracy, AUROC and F1 at fixed 0.5 are secondary. Every warning, failure,
trial, data/source digest and selection is retained. There are no speed,
memory, certification, LP, PDE or novelty claims from this comparison.

`tabular/requirements.lock`; do not change the lab runtime lock.

python -m tabular.profile_study --output artifacts/profile_study.json

#### Interpretation boundaries

The logistic bell is a scaled ordinary logistic density. An independent
ordinary-PyTorch formula matches its values, gradients and twenty AdamW
updates exactly in the focused check. A benefit of this profile would therefore
not demonstrate differentiation of an exact equality predicate or a need for
an omnibias-specific engine. Its tails and curvature are inductive-bias choices.

The inherited geometry uses established Hermite/Stein-score methods and
training-estimated elliptical density models. This study evaluates the full
recipe in a planted class, not a new mathematical branch, arbitrary symbolic
discovery, general PDE/LP solution, or a real-data tabular benchmark. All six
cases and all failures remain in JSON. No timing or memory claim follows.

#### Reproduction

```bash

python -m tabular.profile_study --output artifacts/profile_study.json
python -m tabular.profile_analysis --input artifacts/profile_study.json --output artifacts/profile_summary.json --report tabular/PROFILE_RESULTS.md
```

The smoke seed 9101 is excluded. Raw source, note, dependency/lock, command

### Oblique-band tabular pilot

This tests learned normalized sigmoid bands, including an attained zero-width
trial, against Gaussian ridge features, a ReLU MLP, TabM, QDA, LightGBM and
CatBoost. Ordinary Torch's same-function control is exactly equal in six
training steps in the regression tests. The package does not create a different
function or gradient by giving that function a collapse interpretation.

The frozen matrix has six numeric binary datasets, three stratified split seeds
and three trials per method. A 60/20/20 split separates training, selection and
testing. Imputation, scaling and TabM embedding bins use training rows only.
Validation log loss selects checkpoints and trials. Test log loss is primary;
AUROC, accuracy and F1 at threshold 0.5 are secondary. No test threshold is tuned.

The synthetic tasks are a noisy oblique slab, the XOR of two oblique slabs, and
an axis-aligned tree rule. Real datasets are sklearn's Breast Cancer, OpenML
Banknote (1462) and Spambase (44). Downloads stay in a local data directory;
JSON provenance records array hashes and OpenML metadata. No private data enter.

This is a small CPU pilot, not the consumer's five-seed best-in-class gate.
Neural models have up to 180 full-batch AdamW steps, validation every five steps
and ten-check patience. TabM uses its official package with numerical embeddings,
mean per-member training loss and averaged inference probabilities, but a reduced
CPU configuration (8 members, two 64-unit blocks, 4-dimensional embeddings).
It is not the authors' recommended 32-member, 512-unit configuration. Trees use
up to 500 boosting iterations and validation early stopping. Three trials is
equal search count, not equal compute or exhaustive tuning. Fit time includes
model construction, optimizer updates and validation, excluding preprocessing.

Band trials have initial (half-width, beta, learning rate) of (0.25,4,0.001),
(0.6,8,0.003), (0,8,0.01). Positive widths are learned through softplus; zero
width is fixed because symmetry makes its first width gradient zero. Gaussian
initial widths are 0.25,0.6,1.2. Both ridge models use 32 learned unit-normal
projections and a 32-unit ReLU head with raw-input skip. The MLP is 64/32 ReLU.
QDA regularization is 0,0.1,0.5; LightGBM leaves are 15,31,63; CatBoost depths
are 4,6,8. Other settings and source hashes are recorded with results.

The comparison uses a separate Python 3.12.13 environment because the lab's
Python 3.14 lock does not provide these optional comparator wheels. Exact
comparison-package versions are in `requirements.lock`; Torch and editable

### Predeclared spectral ridge study

This follows a negative random-initialization band pilot. Its purpose is to
separate useful geometry initialization from an advantage of a collapsed profile.
The first pilot's source, data and results remain unchanged. This note and the
new runner are hashed before the first matrix result; subsequent results belong
in a separate report, not in this protocol.

#### A concrete higher-order connection

Let X be standard multivariate Gaussian, u,v be orthonormal directions, and
a=Phi^-1(3/4). Put q(t)=2*1{|t|<a}-1 and Y=1{exactly one of the two bands holds}.
Then Y-1/2=-(1/2)q(u.X)q(v.X). Independent sign-flip label noise eta multiplies
the centered conditional expectation by 1-2eta. Gaussian symmetry and E[q]=0 give:

- E[X|Y=0]=E[X|Y=1]=0;
- Cov(X|Y=0)=Cov(X|Y=1)=I;
- the population SAVE matrix is zero, so second-order class geometry is blind.

But the mixed fourth Hermite coefficient is

    c = E[(Y-1/2) H2(u.X) H2(v.X)]
      = -8 (1-2eta) a^2 phi(a)^2 != 0.

Here H2(t)=t^2-1 and phi is the standard Gaussian density. Integration of
(t^2-1)phi(t) over [-a,a] gives -2a phi(a), proving the expression. The only
nonzero fourth-order tensor entries in the u,v basis are permutations of 1122.
Contracting with a direction r twice gives, in that basis,

    C_r = c [[(r.v)^2, 2(r.u)(r.v)],
             [2(r.u)(r.v), (r.u)^2]].

It has rank two whenever both projections of r are nonzero. Its range is the
decision subspace. This is an exact population statement, not a finite-sample
identification guarantee. Eigenvectors identify the span, not the individual
normals. In that span the directional fourth moment has fourth angular harmonic

    T(theta) = (3c/4) [1-cos(4(theta-theta0))].

Eight equally spaced angles isolate the cosine/sine coefficients, even in the
presence of lower harmonics. Their phase locates the axes modulo pi/4; an
eight-direction grid includes the true normals despite that ambiguity. A zero
harmonic amplitude is unidentified and is reported as such.

For Gaussian input Z, the fourth score contraction can be evaluated without a
fourth-order tensor. With s=r.Z,

    H4(Z)[.,.,r,r] = (s^2-||r||^2)(ZZ^T-I)
                    -2s(Zr^T+rZ^T)+2rr^T.

Weighted sample means require O(L*n*d^2 + L*d^3) arithmetic for L contractions
and spectral kernels, and O(n*d+d^2) working memory. No empirical speed claim
against a strong alternative follows from these counts. The code never forms
the full d^4 tensor. Independent fourth Gaussian derivatives test this identity.

These are applications of established sufficient-dimension-reduction and
score-function ideas, not a claim to invent the derivative/moment relation:

- [Weisberg, Dimension Reduction Regression in R](https://www.jstatsoft.org/article/view/v007i01)
  implements SIR, SAVE and principal Hessian directions.
- [Janzamin, Sedghi and Anandkumar, Score Function Features for Discriminative Learning](https://arxiv.org/abs/1412.6514)
  uses matrix/tensor score features and their differential identities.

The discontinuous target's moment identity does not supply a pointwise gradient
of a hard decision. A weak/distributional interpretation or smooth approximation
justifies integration by parts; the finite sample estimator uses observed labels.

#### Frozen comparison

Five datasets: fresh oblique slab, balanced XOR, fresh axis-aligned rule, public
OpenML Ionosphere (59) and Sonar (40). The three synthetic generation seeds are
1009,1013,1031, absent from the first pilot. The XOR has 8,192 rows; the other
synthetic tasks have 4,096 rows and eight features. All have 3% independent label
flips. No planted direction is supplied to any model or initializer.

There are three stratified 60/20/20 split seeds (61,73,89), three trials per
method, validation log-loss selection and one test evaluation per selected
model. Training-only imputation/scaling precedes initialization. Test log loss
is primary; AUROC, accuracy and F1 at 0.5 are secondary. Splits overlap, so
differences are descriptive, not a statistical significance claim.

Five initializers are crossed with two profiles:

1. Eight random directions in the full feature space.
2. Eight directions in a random two-dimensional plane.
3. Two leading SAVE directions after rank-truncated training whitening.
4. Two leading directions of the squared fourth-score-contraction kernel.
5. The same fourth-score span, rotated by its fourth angular harmonic phase.

Whitening discards covariance eigenvalues <=1e-6 of the largest. At least two
retained dimensions are required; rank and resource refusals are recorded.
The score kernel averages 12 random contractions with seed-fixed unit normals.
For spectral methods, directions are formed in whitened coordinates, mapped
back to standardized input coordinates and normalized. Normals are not frozen
during neural training. Each of eight directions has four training projection
quantile centers (0.2,0.4,0.6,0.8), giving 32 features. No validation/test rows
or labels enter initialization. Real-data Gaussianity is not assumed: score
initialization there is a heuristic with no recovery theorem.

The collapsed profile is sech^2(8z/2), with fixed zero bias spacing. The Gaussian
profile has a fixed scale matching its initial full width at half maximum.
The two profiles have identical parameter counts, head initialization and input
skip connections. Both train normals, centers and a 32-unit ReLU head. Keeping
both scales fixed prevents an extra Gaussian width parameter from confounding
this comparison. A learned-width Gaussian and a learned finite-width band are
also included as separate stronger controls from the first pilot's runner.

The other controls are the same MLP, official small TabM, QDA, LightGBM and
CatBoost recipes used previously, trained afresh on these tasks. There are
17 model variants, 255 selected-model evaluations and 765 planned trial attempts.
Three trials is equal search count, not equal compute or exhaustive tuning.
Neural learning rates are 0.001,0.003,0.01; training lasts up to 180 full-batch
AdamW steps with validation every five and ten-check patience. TabM remains
reduced to eight members, two 64-unit blocks and four-dimensional numerical
embeddings. Tree controls use up to 500 iterations and validation early stopping.

All failures, preprocessing source hashes, comparator versions, optional lock,
matrix command, data hashes and source/note digests are retained. Initializer
setup and fitting costs are separate. No comparative speed claim is planned;
the question is whether initialization helps, and whether a benefit is specific
to the collapsed profile. The Python 3.12 comparator environment and immutable
base runner are described in `README.md` and `requirements.lock`.

```bash
python -m pytest tests/test_spectral_ridge.py -q
python -m tabular.spectral_ridge --download --data-dir /path/to/public-data
python -m tabular.spectral_ridge --data-dir /path/to/public-data --output artifacts/spectral_ridge.json
```

Resume requires matching source/note, lock, dependencies, command and data.
This is a lab experiment, not a new omnibias public API or a best-in-class gate.

### Spectral geometry: completed pilot

The frozen primary matrix attempted 765 trials and produced 249 successful
selected-model test evaluations out of 255 records. Twenty-one trial attempts
failed; six selections had no viable candidate. All failures remain in the raw
artifact. A separate post-failure supplement adds 54 trials and 18 successful
selections, retaining the original results unchanged. Total: 819 trial attempts,
267 successful selected-model evaluations and 21 failed trial attempts.

The supplement drops training-constant columns before the original TabM recipe
on Ionosphere, and runs official eigen-solver QDA with shrinkage auto/0.1/0.5
on all five tasks. These are additional valid comparators, not silent replacements
for the frozen recipes. The supplement was fixed after diagnosing failures and
before observing supplement test scores. It is not part of the original protocol.

Mean held-out log loss over three splits; lower is better:

| Dataset | Collapsed random | Collapsed score4+phase | Matched Gaussian score4+phase | Best other tested recipe |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | --- |
| fresh_slab | 0.281144 | 0.234775 | 0.236077 | tabm: 0.225304 |
| balanced_xor | 0.443425 | 0.249009 | 0.251942 | mlp: 0.282399 |
| fresh_axis | 0.424574 | 0.349020 | 0.373119 | lightgbm: 0.151605 |
| ionosphere | 0.245552 | 0.248331 | 0.243881 | tabm_constant_drop: 0.202335 |
| sonar | 0.384057 | 0.390552 | 0.555873 | tabm: 0.365011 |

Fourth-order initialization helps both profiles on balanced XOR: collapsed
log loss improves from 0.443425 to 0.249009; the matched Gaussian reaches
0.251942. The 0.002933 mean profile gap is small, and the Gaussian wins one
of three paired splits. No significance claim is supported. The fourth-order
initialization gain is much larger than the difference between these profiles.

Training-only replay confirms the intended geometry mechanism: on balanced XOR,
SAVE has mean decision-subspace sine error 0.9774, versus 0.1779 for the
fourth-score method. The phase version has mean maximum normal cosines 0.9937
and 0.9864. Planted normals are used only in post-run diagnostics, never supplied
for training or selection. Phase is not uniformly beneficial on other tasks.

The new kernels are not shipped APIs. SAVE, score/Hermite learning, fourth-order
ICA and angular phase methods have existing literature. The 2025 Generative
Leap paper (https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.05500) gives stronger spectral U-statistic
estimators not compared here. Kernel SVM, full-size TabM and RealMLP are also
not covered. These results do not establish a new method, general superiority,
an LP complexity improvement or an arbitrary PDE solver.

The mathematical note in the main repository proves that m independent balanced
band bits first appear at total Hermite degree 2m. Independent quadrature checks
cover m=1 through 4 and the moment estimator variance. This connects higher
orders with hidden interactions, while exposing growing sampling cost. It is
not a universal lower bound or a newly invented calculus.

refusals, phase recovery, parity moments, parameter parity, data separation,
summary failure handling and baseline construction. Lint passes. The main

### Stronger-control timing supplement

The first pair-kernel timing grid motivated an additional exact tensor control.
It computes only unique sorted fourth moments, rather than a full symmetric
pair Gram, and uses sparse Wick corrections. A compressed tensor unfolding
weights each sorted triple by the square root of its permutation multiplicity.
It avoids reconstructing a redundant full d^4 tensor. Its values are checked
against independent full-tensor and pair calculations with signed weights.

The full original 16-row grid is repeated; no favorable rows are selected.
Twelve runtime perturbations and interleaved method order balance comparisons
among three or four implementations. Both existing tensor controls remain
where their resource budgets permit them, alongside the new unique-moment
control. The fastest measured tensor implementation is the comparison for
each row. Two warmups, float64 CPU, one BLAS thread, input perturbation 1e-4,
both binary label kernels, relative Frobenius tolerance 2e-10 and all refusal
states follow the original protocol. No learning-accuracy, generic speed,
GPU, compilation, gradient, memory-ratio or mathematical-novelty claim follows.

This is the complete source note at compilation time. Its original experiment date, protocol, limitations and historical status apply; later corrections in the overview and subsequent audit notes take precedence. Heading levels, line endings, outer document spacing and source-relative Markdown links are normalized here; code and mathematical expressions are preserved.

### Frozen Hermite estimator and geometry-to-rule study

This study follows the spectral-initialization pilot without editing that pilot.
It tests sampling-diagonal removal, a fuller literature baseline and direct rule
prediction on fresh data. Source and this protocol are hashed before collection.

#### Literature baseline and algebraic checks

The reference is [Damian, Lee and Bruna, The Generative Leap](https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.05500v1),
Algorithm 1 and Equation (5). The implementation covers one stage, degrees two
and four, binary labels, rank two and a label RBF kernel with bandwidth one.
It does not reproduce the sequential Algorithm 2 or certify its finite-sample
assumptions. The paper uses normalized Hermite tensors: h4=He4/sqrt(24).

For scalar label weights t=2y-1, form the mean flattened tensor F and remove
same-observation products:

    V = F F^T
    U = [n^2 V - sum_i t_i^2 Phi_i Phi_i^T] / [n(n-1)].

For binary labels, the RBF label kernel equals alpha+beta*t_i*t_j, where
alpha=(1+exp(-1/2))/2 and beta=(1-exp(-1/2))/2. Its U-statistic is therefore
alpha*U_constant+beta*U_sign. This is the paper baseline, not the sketch below.
Eigenvectors use the largest algebraic eigenvalues. Finite U matrices can be
indefinite; no positive-semidefinite clipping conceals this sampling behavior.

The full mean tensor is computed from blocked weighted Gram matrices of x_a*x_b
features and Wick corrections. This retains d^4 mean coefficients but avoids
per-observation tensors and explicit n^2 sample-pair enumeration. Full degree
four is capped at d<=32 and n<=16,384. One temporary block has 256 observations.

The same-observation correction has a closed form. With r=||x||^2,

    Phi4(x) Phi4(x)^T = [A(r,d) xx^T + B(r,d) I] / 24
    A = r^3 - 12r^2 + (3d+36)r - 6d - 24
    B = 3r^2 - 6r + 3d + 6.

One derivation uses S_k(x,z)=<He_k(x),He_k(z)> and the Gaussian generating
kernel sum_k S_k t^k/k!. Differentiate S5 once in each argument, subtract
5*S4*I, and divide by 20. Evaluating at z=x gives the unnormalized contraction;
division by 24 supplies the paper's normalization. Independent tensor entries
and explicit ordered-pair sums test every normalization and correction term.
This is an algebraic implementation identity, not an outward rounding proof
or an invention of Hermite tensor estimation.

The cheaper sketch uses 12 seed-fixed unit directions. Each fourth tensor is
contracted twice along a direction. We compare squaring that sample mean with
removing its diagonal terms. The pointwise score matrix is rank two plus an
identity term; its square is accumulated with weighted Gram and outer products.
This sketch does not have the paper's full-tensor guarantees.

#### Data and assumptions

Four cases, with three independent generation seeds (2111,2129,2137):

| Case | Input law | Dimension | Training observations | Gate |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: | --- |
| xor8 | Standard Gaussian | 8 | 2,048 | XOR |
| xor32 | Standard Gaussian | 32 | 8,192 | XOR |
| and16 | Standard Gaussian | 16 | 4,096 | AND |
| student_xor16 | Spherical Student-t, five degrees of freedom, covariance I | 16 | 4,096 | XOR |

Each case has 1,024 fresh validation and 4,096 fresh test observations. A fresh
rank-two orthonormal frame is drawn for each case/seed. Clean labels combine
the two symmetric bands |w_j.x|<Phi^-1(3/4), followed by 3% independent flips.
No planted normal enters estimation, rule fitting, neural initialization or
selection. They are used only for diagnostic subspace errors. The Gaussian
input law, zero mean and identity covariance are part of the statistical model;
we do not sample-whiten or empirically center the estimator inputs. This avoids
claiming iid unbiasedness after fitting a transformation to those same rows.

The Student-t case deliberately violates Gaussian score assumptions and lacks
finite eighth moments. Its observed behavior is a stress test, not a theorem
about non-Gaussian inputs. Truth, validation and test labels are never used to
choose or change the frozen algorithm or grid after test outcomes are observed.

#### Estimators and predictors

Eight estimated rank-two subspaces: random, SAVE, fourth-score sketch V and U,
full fourth-score V and U with sign labels, and the paper's label-RBF U at
degrees two and four. Shared intermediate costs are recorded as such. Timing
does not establish independent pipeline speed ratios or time-to-target gains.

Each estimated subspace seeds a **restricted two-band rule learner**. A training
fourth angular phase is followed by eight angle offsets j*pi/16 and training
absolute-projection quantiles 0.4,0.5,0.6. These give 24 candidate partitions.
For each, all four binary cells learn probabilities (positives+1)/(count+2)
from training labels. Validation log loss selects the partition. Neither XOR
nor AND is supplied to that learner: its four probabilities can learn either
gate. But rank two and this symmetric-band grammar are supplied. This is not
general symbolic discovery, an arbitrary PDE solver or a new LP algorithm.

Neural controls use the previous frozen trainer, up to 180 full-batch AdamW
steps, learning rates 0.001,0.003,0.01, checkpointing every five and ten-check
patience. Collapsed sech-squared and fixed Gaussian profiles have matched
initial FWHM and parameter counts. Both are initialized from either a random
plane or the full degree-four paper estimator. Both initializers use a training
angular phase and training projection centers; normals remain trainable.
An ordinary MLP and RBF SVM are additional controls. SVM C is 1,10,100,
gamma='scale', with training-only internal probability calibration. It has
100,000 maximum solver iterations and a 512 MiB cache. Non-convergence is a
retained failed trial. All trial selection uses validation log loss.

There are 12 independent case/seed draws and 14 selected predictors per draw:
168 planned test evaluations. Rule learners consider 2,304 partitions in total;
neural/MLP/SVM controls attempt 216 fits. These are unequal tuning/compute
budgets and different model assumptions; no unrestricted superiority claim
follows. Test log loss is primary, with accuracy, AUROC and F1 at 0.5 secondary.
Raw failures, warnings, eigenvalues, shared setup times, data hashes, source,
dependency versions and the comparator lock are retained. Comparators use the
existing optional Python 3.12 environment; no lab runtime lock is changed.

```bash
python -m pytest tests/test_hermite_ustat.py tests/test_ustat_study.py -q
python -m tabular.ustat_study --output artifacts/ustat_study.json
```

The source/note/dependency and generated-data checks guard resume. Study
changes require a fresh output. Results belong in a separate report so this
protocol remains the original hashed precollection artifact.

Source: [omnibias-lab/tabular/USTAT_RESULTS.md](/home/vardan/dev/projects/omnibias_projects/omnibias-lab/tabular/USTAT_RESULTS.md). Original SHA256: `325ce8fd19deb8877c7f480782943a6b44fe0e12f4f055fe738a199663b83f7c`.

Heading levels, line endings, outer document spacing and source-relative Markdown links are normalized here; code and mathematical expressions are preserved.

### Hermite geometry, direct rules and equivalent matrix kernels

This is the completed report for [the frozen learning protocol](/home/vardan/dev/projects/omnibias_projects/omnibias-lab/tabular/USTAT.md),
[the original timing grid](/home/vardan/dev/projects/omnibias_projects/omnibias-lab/tabular/PAIR_KERNEL.md) and its separately frozen
[stronger-control supplement](/home/vardan/dev/projects/omnibias_projects/omnibias-lab/tabular/STRONG_PAIR_KERNEL.md). None of the original
protocols is rewritten after looking at its outcomes. The literature baseline
is one stage of Algorithm 1 in [Damian, Lee and Bruna (2025)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.05500v1):
degrees two/four, rank two and binary RBF labels with bandwidth one. It is not
a reproduction of the sequential Algorithm 2. Both scalar-transformed labels
and kernel-valued labels belong to that paper's framework.

#### Learning outcomes

All 168 selected-model test evaluations completed, on four synthetic tasks
with three independent data draws each. There were 2,304 candidate rule
partitions and 216 neural/MLP/SVM trial attempts. Three SVM C=100 trials on
Student-t failed to converge at 100,000 iterations; their failures remain in
the raw records. Other trials supplied successful selected SVM models.

Entries below are mean test log loss. Smaller is better; three draws do not
support a general significance or state-of-the-art claim.

| Case | rule:full_v | rule:full_u | rule:paper_u4 | collapsed_random | collapsed_paper4 | gaussian_paper4 | mlp | svm |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| xor8 | 0.394672 | 0.374894 | 0.605900 | 0.680733 | 0.305718 | 0.316040 | 0.373056 | 0.587541 |
| xor32 | 0.644811 | 0.570745 | 0.691584 | 0.696415 | 0.675416 | 0.679072 | 0.694190 | 0.693119 |
| and16 | 0.367394 | 0.336067 | 0.499660 | 0.370106 | 0.239593 | 0.243305 | 0.290090 | 0.376029 |
| student_xor16 | 0.689651 | 0.686379 | 0.689815 | 0.651150 | 0.659328 | 0.696874 | 0.459740 | 0.669803 |

Removing same-observation terms improves the sign-label full-tensor estimator.
On xor32 its mean subspace sine error drops from 0.4442 to 0.2896; direct-rule
test log loss drops from 0.6448 to 0.5707. The fixed-bandwidth RBF label kernel
adds a constant-label tensor term that is zero in the Gaussian population but
adds sampling noise; it is weaker in these finite samples. This is a comparison
between literature estimators, not a new estimator beating that paper.

The neural initialization uses only the RBF degree-four estimator, not the
better-performing scalar-label U estimator. The study therefore does not test
the strongest observed geometry as a neural initializer. Matched Gaussian and
collapsed profiles are close on the Gaussian cases. SAVE plus the direct rule
has mean log loss 0.2703 on AND, better than the degree-four direct rules.
The ordinary MLP wins the Student-t case, where Gaussian-score recovery fails.

The rule learner is supplied rank two and a symmetric two-band grammar. It
fits four cell probabilities and selects 24 angle/quantile partitions using
validation labels. It is not general symbolic regression. Neural and SVM
models get three trials; compute and model assumptions differ. The small
SVM grid and retained nonconvergence prevent a broad kernel-method claim.
Known Gaussian input mean/covariance are supplied; no sample whitening or
planted normal enters training. This is not evidence of generic superiority
over modern tabular methods, already tested separately in the spectral pilot.

#### Same matrix through sample pairs or tensor moments

`hermite_pair_kernel.py` evaluates the same full fourth-Hermite U matrix with
blocked sample pairs and polynomial inner products. It needs O(n^2*d+n*d^2)
arithmetic and O(block*n+d^2) auxiliary storage beyond the input, instead of
retaining a fourth tensor. This is an algebraic implementation of an existing
statistical estimator, not an invention of score features or tensor kernels.

The initial timing grid motivated a stronger control: `unique_moment_control.py`
computes only sorted unique fourth moments and a multiplicity-weighted tensor
unfolding. It avoids the earlier control's redundant pair Gram. The table below
uses the fastest of this control, the symmetric pair-Gram tensor control and,
where bounded, the original dense tensor control. The full 16-row grid is
retained; results from the initial grid are not substituted for this supplement.

| N | D | Label kernel | Fastest tensor control | Tensor / pair median |
| ---: | ---: | --- | --- | ---: |
| 256 | 8 | sign | dense_tensor | 0.502 |
| 256 | 8 | rbf | dense_tensor | 0.830 |
| 2048 | 8 | sign | symmetric_tensor | 0.025 |
| 2048 | 8 | rbf | symmetric_tensor | 0.039 |
| 256 | 16 | sign | unique_tensor | 1.706 |
| 256 | 16 | rbf | unique_tensor | 3.110 |
| 2048 | 16 | sign | unique_tensor | 0.092 |
| 2048 | 16 | rbf | symmetric_tensor | 0.188 |
| 256 | 32 | sign | unique_tensor | 10.301 |
| 256 | 32 | rbf | unique_tensor | 16.291 |
| 2048 | 32 | sign | unique_tensor | 0.586 |
| 2048 | 32 | rbf | unique_tensor | 1.104 |
| 256 | 64 | sign | unique_tensor | 102.018 |
| 256 | 64 | rbf | unique_tensor | 149.929 |
| 2048 | 64 | sign | unique_tensor | 4.640 |
| 2048 | 64 | rbf | unique_tensor | 8.580 |

Ratios above one favor pairs. At N=2,048,D=64, the pair implementation takes
48.1 ms (sign) and 53.4 ms (RBF), versus 223.1 and 458.6 ms for the strongest
measured tensor controls: 4.64x and 8.58x. At N=2,048,D=8 it is 39.4x and
25.9x slower. The large small-N/high-D ratios do not show that those samples
suffice for useful recovery. This is a representation trade-off, not a universal
speedup or a reduction in statistical sample complexity.

CPU float64, one BLAS thread, two warmups and twelve distinct perturbed runtime
inputs per row were used. Interleaved method order is balanced. Maximum observed
relative Frobenius disagreement is 4.74e-14.
This numerical comparison is not a floating-point enclosure. These are matrix
formation times, with no GPU, gradient, compilation, memory-ratio, learning
accuracy or time-to-useful-prediction claim. Algebraic novelty is unchecked.

#### Exploratory radial scores

After the frozen learning outcomes, a separate training-only probe evaluates
radial density scores. It scores no validation/test predictions. For a density
p(x)=psi(r), r=||x||^2, integration by parts suggests score matrices
Hess(p)/p and Hess(Delta p)/p; each has the form A(r)xx^T+B(r)I. Gaussian degree
four is the partial trace of He4, with A=r-d-4 and B=d+2-r. Student-5 scores
use its known covariance-I density, not an estimated input law. Independent
autodiff-of-density oracles test both orders and both laws.

| Case | Gaussian degree 2 | Gaussian degree 4 | Student-5 degree 2 | Student-5 degree 4 |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| xor8 | 0.958186 | 0.633419 | 0.548185 | 0.288757 |
| xor32 | 0.998845 | 0.987272 | 0.999553 | 0.999912 |
| and16 | 0.186563 | 0.348842 | 0.151664 | 0.263235 |
| student_xor16 | 0.994171 | 0.979793 | 0.228785 | 0.289754 |

Values are mean planted-subspace sine errors, not prediction losses. The
Student-5 degree-two score improves Student-t geometry from Gaussian degree
four's 0.9798 to 0.2288. All these radial variants fail xor32 at this sample
size. Using a Student score on Gaussian data is a deliberately mismatched
weighting probe, not a valid Gaussian Stein identity. It cannot be interpreted
as an unbiased estimate of that Gaussian derivative moment.

These mechanisms have close precedents in [score-function features](https://arxiv.org/abs/1412.6514),
[principal Hessian directions](https://doi.org/10.1080/01621459.1992.10476258),
and [generalized pHd for elliptical inputs](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jmva.2018.07.006).
The next confirmatory question is whether training-estimated density parameters
and lower-order score choices improve fresh held-out prediction versus matched
ordinary profiles and conventional estimators. The present probe does not answer it.

#### Reproduction and preservation

Raw files: `artifacts/ustat_study.json`, `artifacts/pair_kernel_benchmark.json`,
`artifacts/strong_pair_kernel.json` and `artifacts/radial_score_probe.json`.
The paper PDF is retained under `artifacts/sources/`. Main-repository reviewed
snapshots normalize machine paths and are not valid raw resume inputs.

```bash
python -m pytest -p no:cacheprovider tests/test_hermite_ustat.py tests/test_ustat_study.py tests/test_hermite_pair_kernel.py tests/test_unique_moment_control.py tests/test_radial_score_probe.py -q
python -m tabular.ustat_analysis --artifact-dir artifacts --output artifacts/ustat_summary.json --report tabular/USTAT_RESULTS.md
```

All 45 focused tests pass. No public primitive, package license or website is
changed by this study. The pair kernel is a standalone NumPy prototype that can
be preserved independently of the larger package stack. The rest is a research
record with explicit positive and negative outcomes, not a new-mathematics claim.

### Verified physical calibration

This experimental consumer implements the user-approved eight-hour study. The
primary task is recovering the unknown coupling in a clamped cubic beam from a
certified integrated observation; sparse point sensors are a separate study.
Existing experiments and stable public APIs are preserved.

#### Environment and commands

The collected run uses the existing CPU comparator environment. No comparator
was installed for this phase. Set one thread and the sibling proof source paths:

```bash
export OMP_NUM_THREADS=1 OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS=1 MKL_NUM_THREADS=1
export CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES='' JAX_PLATFORMS=cpu JAX_ENABLE_X64=1
export PYTHONPATH="$PWD:$PWD/../omnibias-research/src:$PWD/../omnibias-geometry/src"
/tmp/omnibias-geometry-comparators/bin/python -m pytest --import-mode=importlib -p no:cacheprovider verified_calibration_research/test_checks.py -q
/tmp/omnibias-geometry-comparators/bin/python -m verified_calibration_research.run --stage all --output artifacts/reproduction_verified_calibration
/tmp/omnibias-geometry-comparators/bin/python -m verified_calibration_research.run --replay --output artifacts/reproduction_verified_calibration
```

Choose a fresh output directory. Individual stages are `checks`, `mathematics`,
`controls`, `references`, `energy`, `points`, and `confirmation`. A complete
stage can be resumed only with matching source, dependency, registration and
lockfile fingerprints. Partial stages require a fresh output directory. The
initial collected run passes `--implementation-start 2026-10-19T05:49:44+00:00`
to include implementation work in its eight-hour ceiling. Reproductions default
to a fresh execution deadline, and resume preserves that deadline.

#### Assurance contract

The state estimate is the proved global monotone-energy bound. Every accepted
state enclosure covers the whole spatial domain; parameter-cell witnesses also
cover their complete coupling interval. Polynomial residuals use an exact
shifted-Chebyshev coefficient norm, independently reconstructed into the original
polynomial. Bernstein bounds enclose field values. This stronger control was
selected before discovery after a coupling-37 smoke case exposed avoidable
Bernstein subdivision cost.

Neural observations use rigorous midpoint Taylor quadrature through fourth
order. Its uncertainty is separate from the state-error estimate and is refined
when necessary. Polynomial candidate integrals are exact rational integrals.
Physical-sensitivity residuals use the same global energy inverse bound.

The scalar integrated observable is strictly decreasing at nonzero forcing.
Recovery brackets both endpoints of the measurement interval's inverse image.
Local conditioning witnesses and all parameter exclusions are independently
replayed. A lower loss alone never constitutes parameter recovery. Measurement
uncertainty can leave a wide feasible interval even when endpoint uncertainty
meets its numerical target.

Sparse sensors use a complete parameter cover without assumed monotonicity.
`CERTIFIED` there means a resolved outer/inner feasible-set cover; existence is
reported separately. Multiple components and unresolved regions are preserved.
A time or precision limit returns `INCONCLUSIVE`.

Reference observations use independently fitted high-precision polynomial
witnesses, with a 10^30 reference snapping denominator. Competing proposals use
10^12 as specified. Reference uncertainty is carried into the measured interval.
Generating parameters are present only in the controller's reference records;
the calibration-worker input contains observations and no generating parameter.
SciPy collocation supplies numerical consistency checks, not continuum proofs.

Cold costs include reduced-basis snapshots and POD construction. Measured batch
costs charge that setup once. Projected amortization at 10 and 100 queries is
labeled as projected. Only complete matrices can promote a candidate, and
confirmation inputs are not constructed until the discovery gate is frozen.

The report records analytic deductions and their assumptions, exact and numerical
checks, source comparisons, all timeouts and unavailable comparators. These are
written mathematical proofs and replayable numerical certificates; no formal
proof-assistant build is claimed.

#### Supplemental audit and failure probes

After the campaign process and its numerical replay have exited, run:

```bash
python -m reports.finalize_verified_calibration artifacts/reproduction_verified_calibration --probe
```

This runs additional input-binding and regularity regressions, then the bounded
higher-order residual-enclosure and uniform point-sensitivity probes only when
no primary candidate qualifies. Each probe has its own source digest and replay
command. Their results remain post-discovery evidence and never change the
frozen primary promotion gate. The finalizer links the standalone report, builds
the documentation and creates source/dependency snapshots.
